SENALT.description: Sensor height in km relative to the WGS-84 ellipsoid at the time of the observation.

SENX.description: Cartesian X position in km at the time of the observation.

SENY.description: Cartesian Y position in km at the time of the observation.

SENZ.description: Cartesian Z position in km at the time of the observation.

FOV_COUNT.description: Total number of satellites in the field of view.

FOV_COUNT_UCTS.description: Number of uncorrelated satellites in the field of view (JCO).

EXP_DURATION.description:
Image exposure duration in seconds. For observations performed using frame stacking or synthetic tracking methods,
the exposure duration should be the total integration time. This field is highly recommended / required if the
observations are going to be used for photometric processing.

NET_OBJ_SIG_UNC.description: Net object signature uncertainty = counts uncertainty / EXP_DURATION.

MAG.description: Measure of observed brightness calibrated against the Gaia G-band.

GEOLAT.description:
Computed estimate of the latitude, positive degrees north. It should be computed based on the assumed slant range
and corresponding viewing geometry. It must NOT be computed from the orbit state.

GEOLON.description:
Computed estimate of the longitude as +/- 180 degrees east. It should be computed based on the assumed slant range
and viewing geometry. It must NOT be computed from the orbit state.

GEOALT.description: Computed estimate of satellite altitude in km at the reported location. It must NOT be computed from the orbit state.

GEORANGE.description: Computed estimate of the slant range in km. It must NOT be computed from the orbit state.

SKY_BKGRND.description:
Average Sky Background signal, in Magnitudes. Sky Background refers to the incoming light from an apparently
empty part of the night sky.

PRIMARY_EXTINCTION.description:
Primary Extinction Coefficient, in Magnitudes. Primary Extinction is the coefficient applied to the airmass
to determine how much the observed visual magnitude has been attenuated by the atmosphere. Extinction, in general,
describes the absorption and scattering of electromagnetic radiation by dust and gas between an emitting astronomical
object and the observer.

PRIMARY_EXTINCTION_UNC.description: Primary Extinction Coefficient Uncertainty, in Magnitudes.

SOLAR_PHASE_ANGLE.description:
The angle, in degrees, between the target-to-observer vector and the target-to-sun vector. Recommend using the
calculation listed in the EOSSA documentation, pg 106 of the EOSSA spec.

SOLAR_EQ_PHASE_ANGLE.description:
The angle, in degrees, between the projections of the target-to-observer vector and the target-to-sun vector
onto the equatorial plane. The convention used is negative when closing (i.e., before the opposition)
and positive when opening (after the opposition).

SOLAR_DEC_ANGLE.description: Angle from the sun to the equatorial plane.

RAW_FILE_URI.description: Optional URI location in the document repository of the raw file parsed by the system to produce this record.

INTENSITY.description: Intensity of the target for IR observations, in kw/sr/em.

BG_INTENSITY.description: Background intensity for IR observations, in kw/sr/um.

DESCRIPTOR.description: Optional source-provided and searchable metadata or descriptor of the data.

ORIGIN.description:
Originating system or organization which produced the data, if different from the source.
The origin may be different than the source if the source was a mediating system which forwarded
the data on behalf of the origin system. If null, the source may be assumed to be the origin.

DATA_MODE.description: Indicator of whether the data is EXERCISE, REAL, SIMULATED, or TEST.

EXERCISE.description: Data collected during an exercise scenario.

CREATED_BY.description: Application user who created the row in the database, auto-populated by the system.

REFERENCE_FRAME.description: EO observations are assumed to be topocentric J2000 coordinates ('J2000') as defined by the IAU, unless otherwise specified.

SEN_REFERENCE_FRAME.description:
The sensor reference frame is assumed to be the International Terrestrial Reference Frame (ITRF),
unless otherwise specified. (ITRF is equivalent to Earth-Centered Earth-Fixed (ECEF) for this purpose).
Lat / long / height values should be reported using the WGS-84 ellipsoid, where applicable.

UMBRA.description: Boolean indicating that the target object was in umbral eclipse at the time of this observation.

PENUMBRA.description:
Boolean indicating that the target object was in a penumbral eclipse at the time of this observation.
This field is highly recommended if the observations will be used for photometric processing.

ORIG_NETWORK.description: The originating source network on which this record was created, auto-populated by the system.

RANGERATE_MEASURED.description: True if measured, false if computed. Required if range-rate is reported.

RA_MEASURED.description: True if measured, false if computed. Required if right ascension is reported.

DECLINATION_MEASURED.description: True if measured, false if computed. Required if declination is reported.

NIIRS.description: National Imagery Interpretability Rating Scale (NIIRS). Ranging from 0 (lowest) to 9 (highest).

METERS_PER_PIXEL.description: Ground sample distance in meters per pixel.

IMAGE_SNR.description: Signal-to-noise ratio of the image. Higher values indicate cleaner imagery.

IMAGE_WIDTH.description: Width of the image in pixels.

IMAGE_HEIGHT.description: Height of the image in pixels.

IMAGE_COMPRESSION.description: Compression type used for the image, e.g., "JPEG", "PNG", "RAW", etc.

IMAGE_COMPRESSION_RATIO.description: Compression ratio used (original size / compressed size), if applicable.

PROCESSED_IMAGE_URI.description: URI to the processed image used for this observation.

IMAGE_AUTO_ENHANCED.description: Flag indicating whether the image was auto-enhanced (e.g., contrast stretch, denoise).

MULTI_FRAME_STACKED.description: True if the observation was taken with multiple frames stacked into one image.

SYNTHETIC_TRACKING_USED.description: True if synthetic tracking was used to create the image.

IMAGE_SHARPNESS.description: Sharpness metric of the image based on the Tenengrad method or variance of Laplacian. Higher values indicate sharper images.

IMAGE_NOISE_STDDEV.description: Noise level of the image, estimated via pixel intensity variance in background regions.

IMAGE_CONTRAST.description: Contrast metric of the image, such as Michelson contrast or RMS contrast.

IMAGE_DYNAMIC_RANGE.description: Dynamic range of the image (max pixel value / min pixel value), indicating tonal spread.

IMAGE_ENTROPY.description: Entropy of the image, representing the richness of information content. Higher entropy suggests higher texture detail.

BACKGROUND_UNIFORMITY.description: Background uniformity metric (e.g., mean gradient in background areas). Lower values indicate more uniform background.

BACKGROUND_MEAN_LEVEL.description: Mean background level, computed from non-object regions in pixel units.

SATURATED_PIXEL_PERCENT.description: Percentage of saturated pixels in the image. Indicates overexposure when high.

DEAD_PIXEL_PERCENT.description: Percentage of dead or zero-value pixels in the image. Indicates sensor defects or underexposure.

PSF_FWHM.description: Estimated Point Spread Function (PSF) Full Width at Half Maximum (FWHM) in pixels. Indicates image blur or focus.

CLOUD_COVER_PERCENT.description: Estimated percentage of cloud cover in the image. Derived using cloud detection algorithms such as Fmask or machine learning classifiers.

CLOUD_DETECTION_CONFIDENCE.description: Confidence score of the cloud detection result, from 0 (low confidence) to 1 (high confidence).

HAZE_PERCENT.description: Estimated percentage of the image obscured by haze or atmospheric scattering effects.

AEROSOL_OPTICAL_THICKNESS.description: Estimated aerosol optical thickness (AOT) at 550 nm, indicating particulate matter in the atmosphere affecting image clarity.

WATER_VAPOR_CONTENT.description: Estimated water vapor content (e.g., total column precipitable water) at the time of imaging, in mm.

SUN_ELEVATION.description: Sun elevation angle at the time of image capture, in degrees above the horizon.

SUN_AZIMUTH.description: Sun azimuth angle at the time of image capture, in degrees from true north.

VIEW_ZENITH_ANGLE.description: View zenith angle (sensor line-of-sight angle from nadir), in degrees.

VIEW_AZIMUTH_ANGLE.description: View azimuth angle (direction of sensor relative to north), in degrees.

OFF_NADIR_ANGLE.description: Off-nadir angle of the sensor at the time of image capture, in degrees.

SWATH_WIDTH_KM.description: Ground coverage width of the image swath in kilometers.

MEAN_TERRAIN_ELEVATION.description: Mean terrain elevation in the image footprint, in meters above sea level.

TERRAIN_ELEVATION_STDDEV.description: Standard deviation of terrain elevation in the image footprint, in meters.

SHADOW_COVER_PERCENT.description: Percentage of the image affected by shadows, derived via topographic or object shadow detection.

SUNGLINT_PRESENT.description: Flag indicating whether sunglint is present in the image (true if high reflectance from water surface due to sun geometry).

SUNGLINT_PERCENT.description: Percentage of image affected by sunglint.

SNOW_ICE_COVER_PERCENT.description: Estimated percentage of snow or ice coverage in the image footprint.

VALID_DATA_AREA_KM2.description: Total area covered by valid data (non-masked, usable imagery) in square kilometers.

RCS.description: Radar cross-section (dBsm)

IN_PROGRESS.description: Chunks remain; NEXT_OFFSET is where the next read starts.

COMPLETE.description: The source was read to its end and every chunk was committed. NEXT_OFFSET equals the total length when the length is known.

FAILED.description: The publisher stopped on an error it did not recover from; FAULT states what happened. The mark stays valid as a resume point.

ABANDONED.description: The publisher abandoned the job deliberately; it is not a resume point and a consumer restarts from offset 0.

INVALIDATED.description: The source changed identity underneath the job (VALIDATOR mismatch), so the position no longer refers to the same bytes. A conforming consumer restarts from offset 0 rather than resuming.

OFFSET_LENGTH.description: Half-open ranges expressed as a start offset and a byte count.

INCLUSIVE_BYTE_RANGE.description: Inclusive first/last byte positions, the convention of ranged transfer protocols: a chunk of `RANGE_FIRST_BYTE`..`RANGE_LAST_BYTE` inclusive.

PART_INDEX.description: The source is delivered as discrete numbered parts and byte offsets are not addressable; CHUNK_INDEX is the only position.

MATCHED.description: The publisher compared validators and they agree; resuming is safe.

MISMATCHED.description: The publisher compared validators and they disagree; the bytes behind the offset are not the bytes that were read.

UNVERIFIABLE.description: The source published no validator to compare. This is NOT a match: a publisher that cannot verify identity says so instead of assuming it.

IRMSource.description:
The source object a job is reading, and the validators that prove a resumed
read is reading the same bytes.

SOURCE_URL.description: Replayable locator of the source object, verbatim.

SOURCE_OBJECT_ID.description:
Source-native object, export, or product identifier verbatim, when the
provider names one independently of its locator.

SOURCE_CID.description:
Content identifier pinning the exact source bytes, when the source is
content-addressed.

MEDIA_TYPE.description: Media type of the source object verbatim as the provider states it.

TOTAL_BYTES.description:
Total length of the source object in bytes. 0 means the provider did not
state a length; it never means an empty object.

ENTITY_TAG.description: Opaque entity validator verbatim as the provider published it.

SOURCE_SHA256.description:
SHA-256 of the complete source object as 64 lowercase hexadecimal
characters, when the provider publishes one. Never computed from a partial
read.

SOURCE_VERSION.description: Provider-stated edition, revision, or release marker verbatim.

VALIDATOR_MATCH.description: What the publisher concluded when it last compared validators.

MATCHED.description: The publisher compared validators and they agree; resuming is safe.

MISMATCHED.description: The publisher compared validators and they disagree; the bytes behind the offset are not the bytes that were read.

UNVERIFIABLE.description: The source published no validator to compare. This is NOT a match: a publisher that cannot verify identity says so instead of assuming it.

VALIDATED_AT.description: RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp of that comparison.

IRMDecodeContext.description:
Everything a resuming reader needs to decode a chunk that does not begin at
offset 0. Required whenever NEXT_OFFSET is past the source's own header.

FORMAT.description:
Format token the decoder dispatches on, verbatim and lowercase, e.g.
`text/csv`. A consumer that does not implement the format refuses the chunk
rather than guessing at a layout.

HEADER_LINE.description:
The source's header line verbatim, exactly as it appeared at offset 0 and
excluding its line terminator. This is the field that makes chunk N>0
decodable; without it a headerless chunk parses to zero rows and looks like
a clean tail.

HEADER_BYTE_LENGTH.description:
Byte length the header occupied at the start of the source, including its
terminator, so a reader can tell a header-bearing prefix from a data row.

COLUMN_NAMES.description:
Column names in source order, when the publisher parsed them. Advisory:
HEADER_LINE is authoritative and a disagreement is resolved in its favour.

CHARSET.description: Character encoding label verbatim as the provider states it.

COMPRESSION.description:
Stream-compression codec applied to the source bytes, verbatim and
lowercase. Empty means the ranged bytes are read as-is. Non-empty means
NEXT_OFFSET is a position in the COMPRESSED stream and DECODER_STATE,
WINDOW and PARTIAL_RECORD are all required to resume.

DECODED_OFFSET.description:
Position in the DECODED stream corresponding to NEXT_OFFSET, when the
source is compressed. 0 with a non-empty COMPRESSION means the decoded
stream has not been advanced.

DECODER_STATE.description:
Serialized, pointer-free image of the decoder at the seam — the state a
codec with no restart point needs in order to have one. Opaque to every
consumer but a decoder whose stamps match exactly. Never partially applied.

DECODER_STATE_FORMAT.description:
Layout identifier of DECODER_STATE, verbatim, naming the decoder struct the
image was taken from. A consumer that does not know the token restarts.

DECODER_STATE_VERSION.description: Version of that layout, verbatim. Any disagreement restarts the job.

DECODER_STATE_BYTE_LENGTH.description:
Byte length DECODER_STATE is expected to have. Carried even though the
vector knows its own size, so a size disagreement is detectable BEFORE the
image is loaded into a differently shaped struct.

DECODER_STATE_SHA256.description: SHA-256 of DECODER_STATE as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.

DECODER_BUILD_ID.description:
Build identifier of the decoder that produced DECODER_STATE, verbatim, so
two builds of one codec version are still distinguishable.

DECODER_STATE_MEDIA_TYPE.description:
Media type of DECODER_STATE, so an unrelated decoder refuses it instead of
misreading it.

WINDOW.description:
The decoder's history window at the seam — the bytes that ARE the codec's
back-reference dictionary. Carried separately from DECODER_STATE because it
is bulk data of a size the codec fixes, not part of the struct image.

WINDOW_BYTE_LENGTH.description:
Byte length WINDOW is expected to have, for the same detect-before-load
reason as DECODER_STATE_BYTE_LENGTH.

WINDOW_POSITION.description:
Offset into WINDOW at which the codec will next write, when the window is
a circular buffer whose contents cannot be interpreted without it.

PARTIAL_RECORD.description:
The bytes of the record that straddles the seam: everything the previous
chunk decoded of a record it could not finish. A resuming decoder prepends
these to the next chunk's decoded output before parsing. Carried as bytes,
not text, because a seam may fall inside a multi-byte character.

IRMChunk.description: One chunk that was read and durably committed.

CHUNK_INDEX.description: Zero-based position of the chunk in the job's read sequence.

BATCH_ID.description:
Publisher-stable batch identifier the chunk's records were stored under,
verbatim, so a consumer can join the mark to the stored rows.

RANGE_FIRST_BYTE.description: First byte of the range that was read.

RANGE_LAST_BYTE.description:
Last byte of the range that was read. Interpreted per RANGE_MODE:
inclusive under INCLUSIVE_BYTE_RANGE, exclusive under OFFSET_LENGTH.

BYTE_LENGTH.description:
Bytes the read actually returned, which may be shorter than the range
requested.

CHUNK_SHA256.description: SHA-256 of the chunk's bytes as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.

RECORDS_DECODED.description: Records the decoder produced from the chunk.

RECORDS_STORED.description:
Records the storage lane reported as durably committed. A chunk whose
stored count is 0 is not marked at all.

RECORDS_REJECTED.description: Records the storage lane rejected or collapsed as duplicates.

ATTEMPTS.description: Number of read attempts this chunk cost, including the successful one.

COMMITTED_AT.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp at which the storage lane
confirmed the commit.

IRMFault.description: The last unrecovered error, carried so a resumed run can refuse to loop.

CODE.description: Publisher-stable error code verbatim.

MESSAGE.description: Human-readable message verbatim; never a substitute for CODE.

CHUNK_INDEX.description: Zero-based index of the chunk the fault occurred on.

CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES.description: Consecutive failed attempts at that chunk.

OCCURRED_AT.description: RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp of the fault.

RETRY_NOT_BEFORE.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp before which a consumer must not
retry. Empty means the publisher states no backoff.

JOB_ID.description:
Publisher-stable identifier of the ingest job. Together with the publishing
key it is the job's identity across every mark it emits.

SEQUENCE.description:
Monotonic version of this mark within JOB_ID. Highest wins per publishing
key. Never reused, never decremented.

PROVIDER_ID.description:
Publisher-stable identifier of the data provider being read, verbatim.
Publisher data: it may name a real provider.

INGESTOR_ID.description:
Reverse-DNS identifier of the ingest module or flow that owns the job, so
two pipelines reading one provider do not share a resume point.

SOURCE.description: The source object and its validators.

IN_PROGRESS.description: Chunks remain; NEXT_OFFSET is where the next read starts.

COMPLETE.description: The source was read to its end and every chunk was committed. NEXT_OFFSET equals the total length when the length is known.

FAILED.description: The publisher stopped on an error it did not recover from; FAULT states what happened. The mark stays valid as a resume point.

ABANDONED.description: The publisher abandoned the job deliberately; it is not a resume point and a consumer restarts from offset 0.

INVALIDATED.description: The source changed identity underneath the job (VALIDATOR mismatch), so the position no longer refers to the same bytes. A conforming consumer restarts from offset 0 rather than resuming.

RANGE_MODE.description: How byte positions in this mark are addressed.

OFFSET_LENGTH.description: Half-open ranges expressed as a start offset and a byte count.

INCLUSIVE_BYTE_RANGE.description: Inclusive first/last byte positions, the convention of ranged transfer protocols: a chunk of `RANGE_FIRST_BYTE`..`RANGE_LAST_BYTE` inclusive.

PART_INDEX.description: The source is delivered as discrete numbered parts and byte offsets are not addressable; CHUNK_INDEX is the only position.

NEXT_OFFSET.description:
Byte offset at which the next read begins, in the SOURCE's own byte stream:
the compressed stream when DECODE_CONTEXT.COMPRESSION is non-empty, in
which case it is a record boundary only in company with the decoder state,
window and partial record. On an uncompressed source it is ALWAYS a
complete-record boundary, corrected backwards from the previous chunk's
byte budget. 0 is a valid value and means the job has committed nothing yet.

NEXT_CHUNK_INDEX.description:
Zero-based index of the next chunk to read. With PART_INDEX addressing this
is the only position.

CHUNK_BYTE_BUDGET.description:
Byte budget the publisher reads per chunk. Records the ceiling the job
actually ran under, which a host may have clamped below the configured one.

DECODE_CONTEXT.description:
Everything needed to decode the chunk at NEXT_OFFSET. REQUIRED in practice
whenever NEXT_OFFSET is past the source's own header; a consumer that finds
it absent there restarts from offset 0 rather than decoding blind.

LAST_CHUNK.description: The chunk this mark was advanced from — the last one durably committed.

CHUNKS_COMMITTED.description: Chunks durably committed by this job so far.

BYTES_COMMITTED.description: Source bytes accounted for by committed chunks.

RECORDS_COMMITTED.description: Records durably committed by this job so far, across every chunk.

TARGET_STANDARD.description:
Four-character standard code of the records this job writes, `$` included,
e.g. `$TBS`. Never a union ordinal.

RECONCILE_MODE.description:
Reconciliation mode the storage lane was called with, verbatim, e.g.
`append`. A chunked job never reconciles per batch: reconciling would delete
every earlier chunk as the next one arrived.

MERGE_POLICY.description: Deduplication or merge policy the job applied, verbatim.

FAULT.description: The last unrecovered error, when there is one.

CREATED_AT.description: RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp at which the job was created.

STARTED_AT.description: RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp at which the first chunk was read.

UPDATED_AT.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp at which this mark was published.
With JOB_ID and SEQUENCE this is the version key; SEQUENCE breaks ties.

COMPLETED_AT.description: RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp at which the job reached COMPLETE.

EXPIRES_AT.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp after which a consumer treats the
mark as stale and re-validates the source before resuming. Empty means the
publisher states no expiry.

TAGS.description: `namespace:value` facets, sorted and deduplicated. See TAG GRAMMAR above.

NOTES.description: Publisher note about this job; never a substitute for a field.

CCT.description:
$CCT — Capability Category Taxonomy.

The ratified set of capability classes that distributable units (modules,
applications, composed flows) are classified under, together with the labels
and routes every consuming surface renders. One published $CCT is the single
source of truth shared by a storefront, a library, a search index and the
unit manifests themselves.

Division of labour: `$CCT` = the category vocabulary and its presentation;
`$PLG` = one module's listing, which cites categories by code; `$APP` = one
application's manifest, which cites categories by code; `$PMM` = which
modules a provider serves; `$STO`/`$STF` = commerce.

TAXONOMY_ID.description: Stable identifier of this taxonomy publication.

VERSION.description: SemVer 2.0.0 version of the taxonomy content.

ISSUED_AT.description: Unix seconds when this taxonomy revision was issued.

CATEGORIES.description:
The ratified categories. Every capabilityClass member a consumer may
encounter SHOULD appear exactly once; a code appearing twice is invalid.

ROLLUPS.description:
Optional per-category item counts as observed over a named catalogue.
Absent means counts are computed by the consumer.

SIGNATURE.description: Signature from the publishing node key over the canonical taxonomy bytes.

PLGAcceptedTypeSet.description:
Accepted schema family for a port. When a port accepts multiple wire
formats (canonical FlatBuffer + aligned-binary), each ALLOWED_TYPE
entry carries its own TAB.FlatBufferTypeRef with the schema identity,
and the enclosing PLGPortManifest advertises both wire formats via
ALLOWED_WIRE_FORMATS. Per SDK contract: a port that advertises
aligned-binary MUST also advertise the canonical flatbuffer fallback
for the same schema and file identifier in the same set.

SET_ID.description: Stable type-set identifier within the port.

ALLOWED_TYPES.description: Specific FlatBuffer types accepted by the set.

ALLOWED_WIRE_FORMATS.description:
Wire formats this set accepts. If ALIGNED_BINARY is present,
FLATBUFFER MUST also be present for the same schemas.

DESCRIPTION.description: Human-readable explanation of the accepted schema family.

PLGPortManifest.description: One input or output port on a method.

PORT_ID.description: Stable port identifier within the method.

ACCEPTED_TYPE_SETS.description: Type sets accepted on this port.

MIN_STREAMS.description: Minimum number of streams that must be connected.

MAX_STREAMS.description: Maximum number of streams that may be connected.

REQUIRED.description: Whether the port must be connected for invocation.

PLGProtocolSpec.description: Protocol handler declared by a plugin.

PLGBuildArtifact.description: Build artifact emitted by the plugin toolchain.

DRAIN_TO_EMPTY.description: Invocation drains to empty before returning.

PLUGIN_ID.description: Plugin ID of the dependency

NAME.description: Function name as exported from WASM

PLGFlowNode.description:
One node in a composed flow graph. A degenerate flow IS a module: a leaf
module leaves the flow-graph fields on PLG empty; a composed flow populates
them. This is how flows reuse the module schema rather than a separate one.

NODE_ID.description: Stable node identifier within this flow

PLUGIN_ID.description: Plugin id of the module this node invokes

METHOD_ID.description: Method id invoked on the module

DISPATCH_MODEL.description:
Dispatch model: empty = linked-direct (in-wasm), "isomorphic" = an
independently instantiated signed WASM node, and "host-capability" = a
generic host adapter.

CONFIG.description: Opaque per-node configuration (FlatBuffer or raw bytes; never JSON)

CANONICAL_TYPE.description:
Canonical SDS identity carried by the edge. NOT `required`: an edge may
be opaque by design (see OPAQUE), and a signer must never be forced to
invent an identity to satisfy the schema. A contract MUST carry exactly
one of CANONICAL_TYPE or OPAQUE = true; a contract with neither, or with
both, is invalid and MUST be rejected by the compiler that signs the flow.

OPAQUE.description:
The edge carries bytes with no SDS identity BY DESIGN — an
application-blind host-capability adapter (an HTTP body, a raw file
chunk) or a timer TICK frame with no payload at all. This is a deliberate
signed assertion of opacity, which is why it is an explicit flag rather
than an absent CANONICAL_TYPE: a missing type must stay distinguishable
from a declared-opaque one. An opaque edge is ineligible for the aligned
route, so ALIGNED_ELIGIBLE MUST be false when OPAQUE is true.

PLGFlowEdge.description: One directed edge wiring a producer output port to a consumer input port.

CONTRACT.description:
Exact identity/layout and compile-time representation policy. NOT
`required`: marking a NEW field of an EXISTING table required makes the
FlatBuffers verifier reject every $PLG buffer written before 1.0.13,
which is a breaking change to a ratified standard. Presence is enforced
where it belongs — the flow compiler MUST refuse to SIGN a flow whose
edges lack a CONTRACT, and a verifier MUST reject a signed flow edge
without one. Buffers predating 1.0.13 stay readable and stay unsigned.

PLGFlowTrigger.description: One flow trigger (e.g. a host timer or HTTP route) that starts a drain.

DEFAULT_INTERVAL_MS.description: Default firing interval in milliseconds (timer triggers)

PLGFlowTriggerBinding.description: Binds a trigger to the node + input port it delivers its frame to.

PRIMARY_CATEGORY.description:
The one ratified $CCT category this module is shelved under. This is the
category a storefront capsule, a library shelf and a breadcrumb show when
exactly one must be chosen. UNSPECIFIED means the publisher did not
classify the module; a consumer renders it ungrouped and never guesses.

This supersedes PLUGIN_TYPE for all storefront, library and search
surfaces. PLUGIN_TYPE remains on the wire and is not removed, but its
`pluginCategory` vocabulary mixes capability families with node-internal
plumbing, carries a legacy vendor-derived member, holds a real family at
ordinal 0, and admits only one value. Canonical migration, applied by a
publisher rewriting an old manifest:
Sensor->SENSORS_AND_COVERAGE, Propagator->PROPAGATION,
Renderer->VISUALIZATION_AND_RENDERING,
Analysis->MISSION_DESIGN_AND_ANALYSIS,
DataSource->DATA_SOURCES_AND_INGEST, EW->ELECTRONIC_WARFARE,
Comms->RF_AND_COMMUNICATIONS, Physics->SPACE_ENVIRONMENT,
Shader->VISUALIZATION_AND_RENDERING, Parser->DATA_SOURCES_AND_INGEST,
Validator->DATA_VALIDATION_AND_QUALITY, Interpolator->PROPAGATION,
Exporter->DATA_SOURCES_AND_INGEST, Foundation->FOUNDATION_AND_MATH,
Infrastructure->NODE_INFRASTRUCTURE, Licensing->COMMERCE_AND_LICENSING,
Storefront->COMMERCE_AND_LICENSING, Publisher->NODE_INFRASTRUCTURE,
Basilisk->PROPAGATION, Maneuver->MANEUVER_PLANNING,
Flow->FLOW_AND_COMPOSITION, Unspecified->UNSPECIFIED.
The mapping is one-way: PRIMARY_CATEGORY is never back-derived into
PLUGIN_TYPE.

UNSPECIFIED.description: No capability class stated. The publisher did not classify the unit. A consumer MUST render an UNSPECIFIED unit as ungrouped and MUST NOT infer a class from the unit's name, description or tags. Display name: "Unspecified".

PROPAGATION.description: Advancing an object's state forward or backward in time under a force model, and interpolating between computed states. Display name: "Propagation".

ORBIT_DETERMINATION.description: Estimating an object's state or model parameters by fitting to observations or ephemerides. Display name: "Orbit Determination".

MANEUVER_PLANNING.description: Planning, targeting and optimizing trajectory changes, including station-keeping, transfers and collision-avoidance maneuvers. Display name: "Maneuver Planning".

CONJUNCTION_ASSESSMENT.description: Screening for close approaches between objects and quantifying collision probability and miss distance. Display name: "Conjunction Assessment".

REENTRY_AND_BREAKUP.description: Atmospheric reentry, decay prediction, fragmentation and debris-cloud evolution. Display name: "Reentry & Breakup".

SENSORS_AND_COVERAGE.description: Sensor modelling and tasking, field-of-regard and access computation, and area or target coverage figures of merit. Display name: "Sensors & Coverage".

TRACKING_AND_OBSERVATION.description: Producing, correlating or associating observations of tracked objects, and maintaining tracks from them. Display name: "Tracking & Observation".

RF_AND_COMMUNICATIONS.description: Radio-frequency link modelling, emitter and band characterization, signal capture handling, and communications planning. Display name: "RF & Communications".

ELECTRONIC_WARFARE.description: Interference, jamming, spoofing and countermeasure modelling. Display name: "Electronic Warfare".

SPACE_ENVIRONMENT.description: Atmospheric density, gravity field, magnetic field, radiation, solar and geomagnetic activity, and ionospheric modelling. Display name: "Space Environment".

DATA_SOURCES_AND_INGEST.description: Acquiring bytes from upstream providers and parsing or exporting them across canonical record formats. Display name: "Data Sources & Ingest".

DATA_VALIDATION_AND_QUALITY.description: Validating records for integrity, physical plausibility, continuity and schema conformance, and scoring data quality. Display name: "Data Validation & Quality".

GROUND_SEGMENT_AND_HARDWARE.description: Ground station operation and control of physical equipment, including antenna rotators, radios and other hardware interfaces. Display name: "Ground Segment & Hardware".

MISSION_DESIGN_AND_ANALYSIS.description: Mission and constellation design, trade studies, performance analysis and report generation. Display name: "Mission Design & Analysis".

FLOW_AND_COMPOSITION.description: Composition of other units into a graph. The unit of distribution is a flow of modules, not a leaf algorithm. Display name: "Flows & Composition".

DATA_STORAGE_AND_QUERY.description: Persisting, indexing and querying records; storage engines and query surfaces. Display name: "Data Storage & Query".

SECURITY_AND_IDENTITY.description: Key custody, signing and verification, authentication, authorization and access control. Display name: "Security & Identity".

COMMERCE_AND_LICENSING.description: Listing, purchase, subscription, entitlement and license enforcement for distributed units. Display name: "Commerce & Licensing".

NODE_INFRASTRUCTURE.description: Node runtime, artifact delivery, registry, publication and peer transport plumbing. Display name: "Node Infrastructure".

FOUNDATION_AND_MATH.description: Foundational mathematics and general-purpose utility libraries consumed by other units rather than run on their own. Display name: "Foundation & Math".

and per-category counting. A module MAY carry several. If nonempty it
MUST include PRIMARY_CATEGORY. Codes MUST NOT repeat. An empty list with
a set PRIMARY_CATEGORY means the module belongs to that one category.

TXSProvenance.description:
Replayable provenance for ONE source's report of ONE facility, emission, or
scheduled transmission.

Every source consulted gets its own entry, including sources that returned
nothing, so a consumer can tell "not looked for" from "looked for and
returned nothing". Source identity is DATA: PROVIDER_ID and AUTHORITY carry
verbatim what that source states about itself.

PROVIDER_ID.description:
Publisher-stable, lowercase identifier for the consulted source, unique
within the publisher's own source registry. Never a display name and
never a URL.

AUTHORITY.description:
The authority under which that source publishes, verbatim as the source
states it: a spectrum regulator, an international coordination register,
a licensee, a monitoring service, or an observer compilation. Never
inferred by the publisher.

SOURCE_URL.description: Replayable URL identifying the source material.

SOURCE_QUERY.description:
The exact query, filter, or request parameters used, so the same rows can
be recovered by repeating the fetch.

LICENSE.description:
Redistribution terms verbatim. Required: there is no encoding for a
redistributed record whose terms are unstated. A source that publishes no
terms is recorded as publishing no terms; unknown terms are never public
domain and never an implied grant.

LICENSE_URL.description: URL of the full licence text as that source publishes it.

ATTRIBUTION.description: Attribution text the licence requires a redistributor to display.

NON_COMMERCIAL_ONLY.description:
The licence forbids commercial use. Rides PER SOURCE because one record
may merge an open-terms lane beside a non-commercial cross-check, and the
strictest consulted lane governs any derived product.

NATIVE_ID.description: This source's own row, record, licence or file identifier, verbatim.

POSITION_AUTHORITY.description:
The class of authority this particular source speaks with about position.
Published per source because a record may merge a regulator lane with a
community lane; the record-level POSITION_AUTHORITY states which class the
PUBLISHED coordinate came from.

published position, and how strongly those reports agreed.

Agreement is CORROBORATION and is never authority: five compilations that

beside POSITION_AUTHORITY, never instead of it.

One documented emission of one facility: a carrier or channel the facility
is stated to radiate, with the power and antenna terms published for it.

A facility radiating many carriers carries many entries; a facility whose

RFB.description:
RF Band Specification

UNITS ARE NORMATIVE. Every frequency field in this table is MHz. Sources
that publish Hz (as open transmitter databases commonly do) MUST divide by
1e6 before encoding; sources
that publish kHz MUST divide by 1e3. BAUD is baud (symbols per second),
never kilobaud. Encoding a Hz value into a MHz field is a defect, not a
convention.

One RFB record carries exactly one LINK_DIRECTION. A transceiver or
transponder is therefore represented as TWO RFB records — one UPLINK and
one DOWNLINK — sharing ID_TRANSMITTER, each carrying its own MODE,
FREQ_MIN, FREQ_MAX and CENTER_FREQ.

MISSION_ELAPSED_SECONDS.description: Seconds from an application-defined mission epoch.

TAI_MINUS_UTC_SECONDS.description: Optional TAI-UTC override in seconds for the source instant.

HAS_TAI_MINUS_UTC.description: Whether TAI_MINUS_UTC_SECONDS should override runtime leap-second data.

DUT1_SECONDS.description: Optional UT1-UTC override in seconds for UT1 conversions.

HAS_DUT1.description: Whether DUT1_SECONDS should override runtime Earth-orientation data.

TRACE_ID.description: Optional caller trace/correlation identifier.

TIMConversionResult.description: Result of a time conversion request.

DELTA_SECONDS.description: Target minus source offset in SI seconds for the requested conversion.

INVALID_INPUT.description: Input epoch or requested representation is invalid.

UNSUPPORTED_TIME_SYSTEM.description: Requested source or target time system is not supported.

LEAP_SECOND_DATA_REQUIRED.description: Conversion requires leap-second data that was not available.

EOP_DATA_REQUIRED.description: Conversion requires Earth-orientation data that was not available.

OUT_OF_RANGE.description: Requested instant is outside the supported conversion range.

ERROR_MESSAGE.description: Optional error detail when STATUS is not OK.

TRACE_ID.description: Caller trace/correlation identifier copied from the request when present.

TIME_SYSTEM.description: Legacy time-system selector retained for existing TIM consumers.

SCLK.description: Spacecraft Clock (receiver) (requires rules for interpretation in ICD)

RFLObstruction.description:
One obstacle interaction on one sample's path. SPARSE: entries exist only
where an interaction was computed, so a clear path is never encoded as a
row of zeroes.

This is the join that makes an arbitrary 3D object a first-class part of
the link budget: MATERIAL_ID names the `$RFS` record whose permittivity,
conductivity, penetration loss and roughness produced LOSS_DB, and
GEOMETRY_REF_ID names the exact mesh, face set, panel or analytic shape
inside it that was hit.

SAMPLE_INDEX.description: Index into the sample arrays this interaction applies to.

OBSTACLE_ID.description: Producer's identifier for the obstacle instance.

MATERIAL_ID.description:
`$RFS.MATERIAL_ID` of the surface that was hit. An obstruction loss with
no material is an unattributed number: a metal panel and a plasterboard
wall of the same size do entirely different things to a link.

VAM_ID.description:
`$VAM` asset identity of the obstacle mesh, when the obstacle is a
reviewed 3D asset.

NORAD_CAT_ID.description:
`$CAT.NORAD_CAT_ID` when the obstacle is a catalogued object (an
occulting spacecraft, a structure on another vehicle). 0 when unbound.

LINE_OF_SIGHT_BLOCKAGE.description: The obstacle blocked line of sight; no energy was propagated through it.

TRANSMISSION.description: Energy passed through the obstacle and paid its penetration loss.

REFLECTION.description: Energy reached the receiver by reflecting off the obstacle.

DIFFRACTION.description: Energy reached the receiver by diffracting around an edge.

SCATTERING.description: Energy reached the receiver by rough-surface scattering.

FRESNEL_INTRUSION.description: The obstacle intruded into the Fresnel zone without blocking the direct ray.

INCIDENCE_ANGLE_DEG.description: Angle between the incident ray and the surface normal, degrees [0-90).

PATH_LENGTH_IN_MATERIAL_M.description:
Path length travelled INSIDE the material, metres. With
`$RFS.ATTENUATION_DB_PER_M` this is what makes penetration loss
reproducible instead of a stated constant.

EXCESS_DELAY_S.description: Extra propagation delay of a reflected or scattered component, seconds.

FRESNEL_CLEARANCE_FRACTION.description:
Fraction of the first Fresnel zone still clear [0-1]. 1 means the zone is
untouched.

DISTANCE_FROM_TRANSMITTER_M.description: Distance from the transmitter to the interaction point, metres.

RFLEndpoint.description:
One endpoint of a link. Identity ONLY — position, antenna geometry and band
capability are NOT copied here; they are joined from the standard named by
ENDPOINT_KIND. A copied position silently goes stale against its source.

ENDPOINT_ID.description: Producer-stable identifier for this endpoint within the record.

SPACECRAFT.description: On-orbit object; joins `$CAT` by NORAD_CAT_ID / OBJECT_ID.

GEODETIC_TRACKING_STATION.description: Geodetic tracking station; joins `$GST` by STATION_ID.

RELAY_PAYLOAD.description: A relay payload acting as an intermediate endpoint of a multi-hop chain.

NORAD_CAT_ID.description:
`$CAT.NORAD_CAT_ID` when the endpoint is an on-orbit object. 0 when
unbound — never a placeholder catalogue number.

RFB_ID.description:
`$RFB.ID` — the band specification (frequency, bandwidth, EIRP, gains,
polarization) this endpoint transmits or receives on.

RFE_ID.description: `$RFE.ID` — the parametric emitter description, when one exists.

IQC_ID.description: `$IQC` capture identifier, when the samples were derived from a recording.

CHANNEL_ID.description: Channel or carrier identifier within the beam.

POLARIZATION.description:
Polarization actually used on this link. Defaults to UNKNOWN explicitly:
`rfPolarization` ordinal 0 is LHCP, so an unset field would otherwise
decode as a real polarization.

RFLModCod.description:
One modulation-and-coding choice available to a link. The table carries
engineering capability only; catalogue or recommendation names belong in
ID / NAME and provenance data, never in the schema vocabulary.

MODCOD_ID.description: Stable identifier within the containing link's MODCOD_SET.

CODE_RATE.description: Information bits divided by coded bits, in (0,1].

REQUIRED_MARGIN_DB.description: Additional implementation margin required before this entry is selected.

MAXIMUM_DATA_RATE_BPS.description: Optional ceiling imposed by framing or implementation, bits per second.

RFLLink.description: One link whose budget is sampled by this record.

LINK_ID.description:
Producer-stable link identifier. Joins `$ACI.ACIInterval.LINK_ID` and
`$LKS.ID` when the same link also has an operational-state record.

USER_BEAM.description: Service link to an end-user terminal.

FEEDER.description: Gateway link carrying aggregated traffic to the network core.

CENTER_FREQUENCY_MHZ.description:
Carrier centre frequency actually used, megahertz — the `$RFB` MHz
convention, NOT the `$IQC` hertz convention. A consumer joining the two
converts explicitly at the join. Band designation is NOT duplicated here:
it is joined from `$RFB.BAND`.

MODULATION.description: Modulation as the producer states it (e.g. "QPSK", "8PSK", "16APSK").

CODING.description: Forward error correction scheme as the producer states it.

CODE_RATE.description: Code rate as a fraction (0-1].

SYMBOL_RATE_BAUD.description:
Symbol rate in baud (symbols per second), NOT kilobaud — the `$RFB.BAUD`
convention.

DATA_RATE_BPS.description: Information bit rate the budget is stated for, bits per second.

THRESHOLD_TERM.description:
Required threshold this link is evaluated against. THRESHOLD_TERM,
THRESHOLD_VALUE, THRESHOLD_UNITS and THRESHOLD_COMPARISON are meaningful
only together; a LINK_MARGIN_DB column without them states a margin
against an unstated requirement and MUST be refused.

OBSTRUCTION_LOSS.description: Loss caused by an obstacle with stated `$RFS` material properties.

SYMBOL_ENERGY_TO_NOISE_DENSITY.description: Energy per transmitted symbol divided by noise spectral density.

BLOCK_ERROR_RATE.description: Error probability for a decoded transport block or frame.

SPECTRAL_EFFICIENCY.description: Delivered information bits per second per hertz.

ACHIEVED_DATA_RATE.description: Data rate delivered by the selected modulation and coding entry.

ACM_MARGIN.description: Margin above the threshold of the selected adaptive entry.

RECEIVER_GROUP_ID.description:
Receiver group this link belongs to. Links sharing a RECEIVER_GROUP_ID
and CHANNEL_GROUP_ID are mutually interfering and MUST be evaluated
together; a producer that shards a link matrix MUST keep a group intact
within one shard.

CONSTELLATION.description: Constellation or network this link belongs to.

SERVICE.description: Operator-facing service or mission designation.

MODCOD_SET.description:
Ordered adaptive modulation-and-coding choices. Per-sample
SELECTED_MODCOD_INDEX indexes this vector for the sample's selected link.

ACM_ENABLED.description: Whether the producer evaluated adaptive selection for this link.

RFLInterferenceContribution.description:
One interfering contribution to one sample. SPARSE: entries exist only
where a contribution was computed, so a dense matrix is never forced into
existence to say "no interference computed".

SAMPLE_INDEX.description: Index into the sample arrays this contribution applies to.

SOURCE_ENDPOINT_ID.description:
Endpoint identifier of the interfering emitter, when it is an endpoint of
this record.

RFB_ID.description: `$RFB.ID` of the interfering emission.

NORAD_CAT_ID.description: Interfering object's catalogue number, 0 when unbound.

INTERFERENCE_POWER_DBW.description: Received interfering power at the victim receiver, dBW.

TOPOCENTRIC_SEPARATION_DEG.description:
Angular separation between the wanted and interfering paths at the
victim receiver, degrees.

SPECTRAL_OVERLAP_FRACTION.description: Fraction of the victim's bandwidth overlapped by this emission [0-1].

POLARIZATION_ISOLATION_DB.description: Polarization isolation applied to this contribution, dB.

ANTENNA_DISCRIMINATION_DB.description: Discrimination applied from the victim antenna pattern, dB.

RFLModelParameter.description:
A named parameter of a model binding, with its unit stated. There is no
encoding for a parameter value without a unit.

TEXT_VALUE.description: Non-numeric parameter value, when the parameter is categorical.

RFLModelBinding.description:
Which model produced one term of the budget. A loss term without a model
binding is an unattributed number: rain attenuation from two different
recommendations differs by decibels, and a consumer must be able to tell
which one it is holding.

TERM.description: The budget term this binding produced.

OBSTRUCTION_LOSS.description: Loss caused by an obstacle with stated `$RFS` material properties.

SYMBOL_ENERGY_TO_NOISE_DENSITY.description: Energy per transmitted symbol divided by noise spectral density.

BLOCK_ERROR_RATE.description: Error probability for a decoded transport block or frame.

SPECTRAL_EFFICIENCY.description: Delivered information bits per second per hertz.

ACHIEVED_DATA_RATE.description: Data rate delivered by the selected modulation and coding entry.

ACM_MARGIN.description: Margin above the threshold of the selected adaptive entry.

MODEL_NAME.description:
Model or recommendation identifier as its publisher states it (e.g. an
ITU-R recommendation number with its revision).

MODULE_ID.description: `$PLG.PLUGIN_ID` / `$PMM.MODULE_ID` of the module that evaluated it.

MODULE_CONTENT_HASH.description: Content hash of the exact artifact that produced the values.

RFLProvenance.description: Where this sample set came from, stated once for the record.

MEASURED.description: Values recorded by instrumentation on a real link.

MODELED.description: Values produced by propagation and RF models.

HYBRID.description: Modelled geometry reconciled against measured RF terms, or vice versa.

SOURCE.description:
The producing system, dataset or measurement campaign. Required: a
budget time series with no stated source is not publishable.

SOURCE_QUERY.description: Replayable query or scenario reference that regenerates this set.

PROPAGATOR_ID.description:
Identifier of the propagator that produced the geometry columns. A record
whose METHOD is MODELED or HYBRID and which carries geometry columns MUST
name it: geometry is only as good as the propagator, and the propagator is
a pluggable choice, never an assumed default.

PROPAGATOR_CONFIGURATION.description: Force model or configuration identifier handed to the propagator.

SAMPLING_STEP_S.description: Uniform sampling step, seconds. Absent when SAMPLE_EPOCHS are irregular.

ENVIRONMENT_DATASET.description:
Weather or environment dataset the atmospheric terms were evaluated
against, when they were not evaluated against a statistical model.

TERRAIN_DATASET.description: Terrain or surface dataset the blockage terms were evaluated against.

COMPUTED_AT.description: Unix ms this set was computed or recorded.

RETRIEVED_AT.description: Unix ms the upstream inputs were retrieved.

LICENSE.description:
Licence the source imposes on redistribution. An empty LICENSE means
UNKNOWN TERMS — never public domain, never a grant to redistribute.

NON_COMMERCIAL_ONLY.description: True when the licence forbids commercial use of this set.

CITATION.description: Attribution the licence requires this record to carry downstream.

MODULE_ID.description:
Primary `$PLG.PLUGIN_ID` / `$PMM.MODULE_ID` that produced this record.
MODELS remains the per-budget-term attribution surface.

MODULE_CONTENT_HASH.description: Content hash of the exact producing WASM artifact.

RFL_ID.description: Stable identifier of this sample set.

SCENARIO_ID.description:
Analysis or scenario grouping identifier shared with the `$ACI` and
`$CVP` products derived from this set.

LINKS.description: Link definitions. SAMPLE_LINK_INDEXES index into this vector.

SAMPLE_COUNT.description:
Number of samples. Every present metric array MUST have exactly this
many entries.

SAMPLE_LINK_INDEXES.description: Index into LINKS for each sample.

SAMPLE_EPOCHS.description:
Sample epochs, seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00 in TIME_SYSTEM. Samples
need not be uniformly spaced and need not be grouped by link, but MUST be
non-decreasing within each link.

TIME_SYSTEM.description:
Time scale SAMPLE_EPOCHS are expressed in. Defaults to UTC explicitly:
`timingStandard` ordinal 0 is GMST, so an unset field would otherwise
decode as sidereal time.

SCLK.description: Spacecraft Clock (receiver) (requires rules for interpretation in ICD)

RANGE_RATE_M_S.description: Range rate, metres per second; positive is opening.

AZIMUTH_DEG.description: Azimuth at the receiving endpoint, degrees east of north [0-360).

ELEVATION_DEG.description: Elevation at the receiving endpoint, degrees above the local horizon.

TRANSMIT_AZIMUTH_DEG.description: Azimuth at the transmitting endpoint, degrees east of north [0-360).

TRANSMIT_ELEVATION_DEG.description: Elevation at the transmitting endpoint, degrees.

DOPPLER_SHIFT_HZ.description:
Doppler shift of the carrier, hertz; positive is closing. Hertz, not the
MHz used for frequencies elsewhere in this record — a shift of a few kHz
on a GHz carrier is destroyed by an MHz encoding.

EIRP_DBW.description: Effective isotropic radiated power toward the receiver, dBW.

TRANSMIT_ANTENNA_GAIN_DBI.description: Transmit antenna gain in the direction of the receiver, dBi.

RECEIVE_ANTENNA_GAIN_DBI.description: Receive antenna gain in the direction of the transmitter, dBi.

GASEOUS_ABSORPTION_LOSS_DB.description: Gaseous (oxygen and water vapour) absorption, dB.

OBSTRUCTION_LOSS_DB.description:
Total loss from 3D obstacles on the path, dB. The per-obstacle detail —
which object, which material, at what angle, through how much of it — is
in OBSTRUCTIONS.

TOTAL_PATH_LOSS_DB.description:
Total of all path terms actually applied, dB. Published as its own column
rather than left to the consumer to sum: a producer that applied a term
this schema has no column for MUST still report an honest total, and the
discrepancy against the itemised columns is then visible.

RECEIVED_POWER_DBW.description: Received carrier power at the receiver input, dBW.

GAIN_TO_NOISE_TEMPERATURE_DB_PER_K.description: Receiving system figure of merit G/T, dB/K.

CARRIER_TO_NOISE_DB.description: Carrier-to-noise ratio C/N in the occupied bandwidth, dB.

ENERGY_PER_BIT_TO_NOISE_DENSITY_DB.description: Energy per bit to noise density Eb/N0, dB.

BIT_ERROR_RATE.description:
Bit error rate as a probability [0-1], NOT an exponent and NOT a
percentage. 1e-6 is encoded 1e-6.

LINK_MARGIN_DB.description:
Link margin against the link's stated threshold, dB. Meaningless without
RFLLink.THRESHOLD_TERM / THRESHOLD_VALUE / THRESHOLD_COMPARISON.

CHANNEL_CAPACITY_BPS.description: Achievable channel capacity, bits per second.

INTERFERENCE_POWER_DBW.description: Aggregate received interfering power, dBW.

CARRIER_TO_NOISE_PLUS_INTERFERENCE_DB.description: Carrier to noise-plus-interference ratio C/(N+I), dB.

OBSTRUCTIONS.description:
Per-interaction obstacle detail, sparse. Each entry names the `$RFS`
material it went through, reflected off or was blocked by.

LIMITING_CONSTRAINTS.description: The single condition that bound the link at each sample.

LIMITING_CONSTRAINT_NOTE.description: Verbatim description required when a LIMITING_CONSTRAINTS entry is OTHER.

PROVENANCE.description:
Provenance of the whole set. Required: an unattributed budget is not
publishable.

COMPUTED_AT.description: Unix ms this record was serialized.

SIGNATURE.description:
Ed25519 signature by the producing `$EPM` over the size-prefixed
FlatBuffer projection with both 64-byte signature payloads zeroed while
preserving their vectors and offsets.

CANONICAL_JSON_SIGNATURE.description:
Ed25519 signature by the producing `$EPM` over canonical JSON with IDL
field order, IDL capitalization, no insignificant whitespace, and both
signature fields omitted.

SELECTED_MODCOD_INDEX.description:
Index into the selected link's RFLLink.MODCOD_SET for each sample.
SELECTED_MODCOD_VALID distinguishes index 0 from no selection.

SPECTRAL_EFFICIENCY_BPS_HZ.description: Spectral efficiency delivered by the selected entry, bit/s/Hz.

ACHIEVED_DATA_RATE_BPS.description: Delivered information rate after adaptive selection, bits per second.

ACM_MARGIN_DB.description: Margin above the selected entry's threshold, dB.

ENERGY_PER_SYMBOL_TO_NOISE_DENSITY_DB.description: Symbol energy to noise spectral density, dB.

BLOCK_ERROR_RATE.description: Decoded block error probability [0-1].

PAPElement.description: One array element and its applied complex weight.

PAPGainCut.description: One one-dimensional gain cut through the synthesized pattern.

PAPNull.description: One requested adaptive null and its achieved result.

HOP_SCHEDULE_ID.description: BEMHopSchedule.SCHEDULE_ID evaluated by this synthesis, when applicable.

SIGNATURE.description:
Ed25519 signature over the size-prefixed FlatBuffer with both 64-byte
signature payloads zeroed while preserving their vectors and offsets.

CANONICAL_JSON_SIGNATURE.description:
Ed25519 signature over canonical JSON with IDL field order and
capitalization, no insignificant whitespace, and both signature fields
omitted.

SIZE.description: Bus size category

WET_MASS.description: Maximum wet mass (with propellant) in kg

DERIVED_FROM.description: Source record this was derived from

GEO_POSITION.description: GEO longitude at event time (degrees east)

MULTI_SOURCE.description: True if fused from multiple sources

TRACK_COMPONENTS.description: Number of components per point (default 3 for X, Y, Z)

ECEF_POS.description: ECEF position as flat array [X0, Y0, Z0, X1, Y1, Z1, ...]

ECEF_VEL.description: ECEF velocity as flat array [VX0, VY0, VZ0, VX1, VY1, VZ1, ...]

ECEF_ACC.description: ECEF acceleration as flat array [AX0, AY0, AZ0, AX1, AY1, AZ1, ...]

LC_POS.description: Local coordinate position as flat array

LC_VEL.description: Local coordinate velocity as flat array

LC_ACC.description: Local coordinate acceleration as flat array

COV.description: Covariance data (21 elements per point for 6x6 lower triangular)

ERR_ELLP.description: Error ellipse data (6 elements per point)

TMSModelParameter.description:
One parameter of the propagation model, stated by name so a model
registry can evolve without schema change.

NAME.description: Parameter name within the MODEL_ID model's own registry, verbatim.

UNITS.description:
Units of VALUE, verbatim. Required: a unitless parameter states so
explicitly (e.g. "1").

TMSIdentifier.description: One identity the track is known by in a named identity scheme.

SCHEME.description:
Identity scheme token, verbatim (the identity system's own name).
Never a field name and never normalized by the publisher.

VALUE.description: The identifier within that scheme, verbatim.

TMSProvenance.description:
Dataset lineage and redistribution terms for one track model state.

Required on every record: a redistributed track whose feed, epoch, and
licence are unstated is not publishable. The standard names no feed,
provider, or site.

DATASET_ID.description:
Publisher-stable, lowercase identifier for the feed or dataset this
state was derived from, unique within the publisher's own dataset
registry. Never a display name and never a URL.

DATASET_NAME.description: The feed or dataset's own name, verbatim as its publisher states it.

DATASET_URL.description: Replayable URL of the feed or dataset as published.

DATASET_EPOCH.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond epoch of the dataset edition or feed
session this state was derived from.

DATASET_CID.description: Content identifier of the exact dataset artifact, when one exists.

SOURCE_URL.description: Replayable URL identifying the source material within the dataset.

SOURCE_QUERY.description: The exact query, filter, or subscription used.

RETRIEVED_AT.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond retrieval timestamp of the observation
this state was updated from.

LICENSE.description:
Redistribution terms verbatim. Unknown terms are never public domain
and never an implied grant.

LICENSE_URL.description: URL of the full licence text as the source publishes it.

ATTRIBUTION.description: Attribution text the licence requires a redistributor to display.

NON_COMMERCIAL_ONLY.description: The licence forbids commercial use.

SHARE_ALIKE.description: The licence obliges derived works to carry the same terms.

NATIVE_ID.description:
The source's own identifier for the track or observation stream this
state was derived from, verbatim.

NATIVE_MODIFIED.description:
RFC 3339 UTC instant the source last modified or emitted the
underlying observation, as the source states it.

ID.description: Publisher-stable identifier for this state record.

TRACK_ID.description:
Publisher-stable identifier of the track this state belongs to, held
constant across every state update of the same track.

ENVIRONMENT.description:
Domain the track moves in. The `$TRK` enum reused verbatim; ordinal 0
is SPACE, so a publisher MUST set this field — it is defaulted to
UNKNOWN explicitly so an unset field can never be read as SPACE.

EPOCH.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond epoch this state is valid at. The
propagation origin: every kinematic field below is stated at EPOCH.

LATITUDE.description: Latitude, decimal degrees on WGS 84, positive north.

LONGITUDE.description: Longitude, decimal degrees on WGS 84, positive east, in [-180, 180].

ALTITUDE_M.description:
Altitude, metres above the WGS 84 ellipsoid. NaN for a surface track
whose source publishes no altitude.

GROUND_SPEED_MPS.description: Speed over ground, metres per second.

VELOCITY_NORTH_MPS.description:
Velocity components, metres per second, local NED-derived axes:
north, east, and up. Published when the source or filter resolves
them; NaN otherwise.

HEADING_DEG.description: Heading, degrees true, [0, 360): the direction the vehicle points.

COURSE_DEG.description: Course over ground, degrees true, [0, 360): the direction it moves.

TURN_RATE_DPS.description: Turn rate, degrees per second, positive clockwise seen from above.

VERTICAL_RATE_MPS.description: Vertical rate, metres per second, positive up.

MODEL_ID.description:
Identifier of the dead-reckoning or motion model that extrapolates
this state, a key into the publisher's model registry. Required: a
state with no model is a position report, which this record is not.

MODEL_PARAMETERS.description: Parameters of that model, named per its own registry.

PROPAGATION_VALID_UNTIL.description:
RFC 3339 UTC instant beyond which the publisher no longer stands
behind propagation of this state.

POSITION_UNCERTAINTY_M.description: 1-sigma horizontal position uncertainty at EPOCH, metres.

INNOVATION_GATE_SIGMA.description:
Gate in standard deviations: an observation whose innovation exceeds
this many sigma of POSITION_UNCERTAINTY_M breached the model and
produced this update.

INNOVATION_GATE_DISTANCE_M.description:
Gate as an absolute distance, metres, when the publisher gates on
distance rather than sigma.

TOLERANCE_M.description:
Publisher's stated tolerance, metres, within which propagation of this
state is considered to agree with truth.

TRACK_STATUS.description:
Track status. The `$TRK` enum reused verbatim; ordinal 0 is ACTIVE,
so a publisher MUST set this field on every record — an unset field
reads as ACTIVE and a consumer cannot distinguish the two.

STALE_AFTER_S.description:
Seconds after LAST_UPDATE_EPOCH at which a consumer MUST mark the
track stale.

DROP_AFTER_S.description:
Seconds after LAST_UPDATE_EPOCH at which a consumer MUST drop the
track.

LAST_UPDATE_EPOCH.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond epoch of the last source observation
that updated this track — the staleness clock origin. EPOCH may lag it
when the publisher re-emits a keepalive state.

IDENTIFIERS.description: Every identity the track is known by, scheme-tagged.

RFB.description:
RF Band Specification

UNITS ARE NORMATIVE. Every frequency field in this table is MHz. Sources
that publish Hz (as open transmitter databases commonly do) MUST divide by
1e6 before encoding; sources
that publish kHz MUST divide by 1e3. BAUD is baud (symbols per second),
never kilobaud. Encoding a Hz value into a MHz field is a defect, not a
convention.

One RFB record carries exactly one LINK_DIRECTION. A transceiver or
transponder is therefore represented as TWO RFB records — one UPLINK and
one DOWNLINK — sharing ID_TRANSMITTER, each carrying its own MODE,
FREQ_MIN, FREQ_MAX and CENTER_FREQ.

RFLObstruction.description:
One obstacle interaction on one sample's path. SPARSE: entries exist only
where an interaction was computed, so a clear path is never encoded as a
row of zeroes.

This is the join that makes an arbitrary 3D object a first-class part of
the link budget: MATERIAL_ID names the `$RFS` record whose permittivity,
conductivity, penetration loss and roughness produced LOSS_DB, and
GEOMETRY_REF_ID names the exact mesh, face set, panel or analytic shape
inside it that was hit.

SAMPLE_INDEX.description: Index into the sample arrays this interaction applies to.

OBSTACLE_ID.description: Producer's identifier for the obstacle instance.

MATERIAL_ID.description:
`$RFS.MATERIAL_ID` of the surface that was hit. An obstruction loss with
no material is an unattributed number: a metal panel and a plasterboard
wall of the same size do entirely different things to a link.

VAM_ID.description:
`$VAM` asset identity of the obstacle mesh, when the obstacle is a
reviewed 3D asset.

NORAD_CAT_ID.description:
`$CAT.NORAD_CAT_ID` when the obstacle is a catalogued object (an
occulting spacecraft, a structure on another vehicle). 0 when unbound.

TRANSMISSION.description: Energy passed through the obstacle and paid its penetration loss.

REFLECTION.description: Energy reached the receiver by reflecting off the obstacle.

DIFFRACTION.description: Energy reached the receiver by diffracting around an edge.

SCATTERING.description: Energy reached the receiver by rough-surface scattering.

Path length travelled INSIDE the material, metres. With

reproducible instead of a stated constant.

EXCESS_DELAY_S.description: Extra propagation delay of a reflected or scattered component, seconds.

FRESNEL_CLEARANCE_FRACTION.description:
Fraction of the first Fresnel zone still clear [0-1]. 1 means the zone is
untouched.

DISTANCE_FROM_TRANSMITTER_M.description: Distance from the transmitter to the interaction point, metres.

Total of all path terms actually applied, dB. Published as its own column

discrepancy against the itemised columns is then visible.

GAIN_TO_NOISE_TEMPERATURE_DB_PER_K.description: Receiving system figure of merit G/T, dB/K.

CARRIER_TO_NOISE_DB.description: Carrier-to-noise ratio C/N in the occupied bandwidth, dB.

ENERGY_PER_BIT_TO_NOISE_DENSITY_DB.description: Energy per bit to noise density Eb/N0, dB.

BIT_ERROR_RATE.description:
Bit error rate as a probability [0-1], NOT an exponent and NOT a
percentage. 1e-6 is encoded 1e-6.

LINK_MARGIN_DB.description:

RFLLink.THRESHOLD_TERM / THRESHOLD_VALUE / THRESHOLD_COMPARISON.

CHANNEL_CAPACITY_BPS.description: Achievable channel capacity, bits per second.

INTERFERENCE_POWER_DBW.description: Aggregate received interfering power, dBW.

CARRIER_TO_NOISE_PLUS_INTERFERENCE_DB.description: Carrier to noise-plus-interference ratio C/(N+I), dB.

OBSTRUCTIONS.description:

material it went through, reflected off or was blocked by.

LIMITING_CONSTRAINTS.description: The single condition that bound the link at each sample.

LIMITING_CONSTRAINT_NOTE.description: Verbatim description required when a LIMITING_CONSTRAINTS entry is OTHER.

PROVENANCE.description:

publishable.

COMPUTED_AT.description: Unix ms this record was serialized.

SPECTRAL_EFFICIENCY_BPS_HZ.description: Spectral efficiency delivered by the selected entry, bit/s/Hz.

ACHIEVED_DATA_RATE_BPS.description: Delivered information rate after adaptive selection, bits per second.

ACM_MARGIN_DB.description: Margin above the selected entry's threshold, dB.

ENERGY_PER_SYMBOL_TO_NOISE_DENSITY_DB.description: Symbol energy to noise spectral density, dB.

BLOCK_ERROR_RATE.description: Decoded block error probability [0-1].

SELECTION_TERM.description: The metric the selection was made on.

OBSTRUCTION_LOSS.description: Loss caused by an obstacle with stated `$RFS` material properties.

SYMBOL_ENERGY_TO_NOISE_DENSITY.description: Energy per transmitted symbol divided by noise spectral density.

BLOCK_ERROR_RATE.description: Error probability for a decoded transport block or frame.

SPECTRAL_EFFICIENCY.description: Delivered information bits per second per hertz.

selection metric with no unit cannot be re-derived or compared.

RUNNER_UP_VALUE.description: Runner-up value of SELECTION_TERM, same units.

TIE_BROKEN_BY.description: Rule applied when the metric tied (e.g. "lowest slant range").

CANDIDATES_EVALUATED.description: Number of candidate servers evaluated, including the winner.

ACIHandover.description: A transition of service between two links.

MAKE_BEFORE_BREAK.description: The successor link was established before the predecessor was released.

BREAK_BEFORE_MAKE.description: The predecessor was released before the successor was established.

HARD.description: Instantaneous switch with no modelled overlap or gap.

SOFT.description: Both links carried traffic simultaneously for the overlap.

SCHEDULED.description: Executed from a schedule rather than triggered by a measured condition.

OVERLAP_S.description:

GAP_S.description: Seconds neither link was usable. Meaningful for BREAK_BEFORE_MAKE.

OTHER.description: The producer states a binding condition this enum cannot express. The verbatim description MUST be preserved in LIMITING_CONSTRAINT_NOTE.

EXECUTED_AT.description:

record's TIME_SYSTEM.

GEOMETRIC_ACCESS.description: Geometry alone permitted the link (mask, range, occultation, beam).

THRESHOLD_SATISFIED.description: The link budget met the stated threshold for the whole interval.

HANDOVER.description: Service moved from one link or server to another.

SCHEDULED_CONTACT.description: A contact booked on a schedule, whether or not it was executed.

INTERFERENCE_EVENT.description: An interval during which interference exceeded a stated criterion.

TRANSMIT_ENDPOINT_ID.description: Endpoints, joined from the same `$RFL` set.

TIME_SYSTEM. An interval with no start is not an interval: a producer that
cannot state it MUST NOT emit the entry. FlatBuffers cannot mark a scalar
required, so this is enforced by the producer, not by the wire.

LOSS_TIME.description:
Loss of signal, same encoding. NaN means the interval was still open at
WINDOW_STOP and was NOT truncated to the window — a consumer must be able
to tell an open pass from one that ended exactly at the boundary.

DURATION_S.description:
Duration in seconds. Published rather than derived so a truncated or
open-ended interval still states the span it actually covers.

THRESHOLD_SATISFIED_START.description:
Sub-interval over which the threshold was met, when it is narrower than
ACQUISITION_TIME..LOSS_TIME. Absent when the whole interval met it or
when no threshold was evaluated.

THRESHOLD_TERM.description:
The requirement this interval is stated against. A margin without these
is a margin against nothing.

OBSTRUCTION_LOSS.description: Loss caused by an obstacle with stated `$RFS` material properties.

SYMBOL_ENERGY_TO_NOISE_DENSITY.description: Energy per transmitted symbol divided by noise spectral density.

BLOCK_ERROR_RATE.description: Error probability for a decoded transport block or frame.

SPECTRAL_EFFICIENCY.description: Delivered information bits per second per hertz.

ACHIEVED_DATA_RATE.description: Data rate delivered by the selected modulation and coding entry.

ACM_MARGIN.description: Margin above the threshold of the selected adaptive entry.

MARGIN_MINIMUM_DB.description: Margin statistics across the interval, dB.

Epoch of MARGIN_MINIMUM_DB, same encoding as ACQUISITION_TIME. The worst
instant of a pass is an operational fact, not a statistic.

DATA_VOLUME_BITS.description:
Data the interval could carry, bits. Bits, not bytes and not megabits:
the rate columns of `$RFL` are bits per second.

LIMITING_CONSTRAINT.description: The condition that bound this interval.

OBSTACLE_BLOCKAGE.description: A 3D obstacle intersected the path. The material that did it is named in RFLObstruction.MATERIAL_ID (`$RFS`).

MATERIAL_PENETRATION.description: The path passed THROUGH an obstacle and paid its penetration loss.

LIMITING_CONSTRAINT_AT.description:

AVAILABILITY_FRACTION.description: Fraction of the interval during which the threshold was met [0-1].

HANDOVER.description: Handover detail, when INTERVAL_KIND is HANDOVER.

index range into the `$RFL` sample arrays named by ACI.RFL_ID.

SAMPLE_COUNT.description: Number of samples that contributed.

ACIProvenance.description: Where this interval set came from.

MEASURED.description: Values recorded by instrumentation on a real link.

MODELED.description: Values produced by propagation and RF models.

HYBRID.description: Modelled geometry reconciled against measured RF terms, or vice versa.

SOURCE.description: Producing system, dataset or campaign. Required.

SOURCE_QUERY.description: Replayable query or scenario reference.

PROPAGATOR_ID.description:

MODELED or HYBRID interval set MUST name it: the propagator is a
pluggable choice and never an assumed default.

MODULE_ID.description: `$PLG.PLUGIN_ID` / `$PMM.MODULE_ID` that computed the intervals.

SAMPLING_STEP_S.description: Sampling step of the underlying grid, seconds.

BOUNDARY_REFINEMENT.description:
How a boundary between two samples was refined (e.g. "none", "linear",
"bisection", "brent"). "none" means the boundary IS a grid epoch.

BOUNDARY_TOLERANCE_S.description:
Worst-case uncertainty of every boundary in this record, seconds. With
no refinement this equals SAMPLING_STEP_S.

MIN_ELEVATION_DEG.description: Minimum elevation applied, degrees, when a single mask governed the set.

COMPUTED_AT.description: Unix ms computed and retrieved.

LICENSE.description:

redistribute.

interval, or choice without decoding a producer-specific map.

WINDOW_START.description:

PPEPositionRecord.description:
A single time-segment record of polynomial coefficients for Cartesian position
(and optionally velocity). Coefficients are stored per axis.

To evaluate position at time t within this record's validity window:
1. Compute normalized time: tau = (t - EPOCH_MID) / EPOCH_HALF_SPAN
where tau is in [-1, +1].
2. Evaluate the polynomial basis of degree (NUM_COEFFICIENTS - 1) using
the coefficients for each axis.

Velocity coefficients, if present, follow the same evaluation procedure.
If HAS_VELOCITY_COEFFICIENTS is false, velocity can be obtained by
analytically differentiating the position polynomial.

EPOCH_MID.description:
Midpoint epoch of this record's validity window (ISO 8601 UTC or TDB).
Together with EPOCH_HALF_SPAN, defines the time interval:
[EPOCH_MID - EPOCH_HALF_SPAN, EPOCH_MID + EPOCH_HALF_SPAN]

EPOCH_HALF_SPAN.description:
Half-span of the validity window in seconds.
The full span is 2 * EPOCH_HALF_SPAN seconds centered on EPOCH_MID.

NUM_COEFFICIENTS.description:
Number of polynomial coefficients per axis.
The polynomial degree is (NUM_COEFFICIENTS - 1).
Typical values: 8-32 for high-fidelity ephemeris fits.

BASIS_TYPE.description: Polynomial basis type for interpreting the coefficient arrays.

CHEBYSHEV.description: Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind T_n(x). Most common for ephemeris fitting due to minimax approximation properties.

LEGENDRE.description: Legendre polynomials P_n(x). Orthogonal on [-1, 1] with unit weight function.

HERMITE.description: Hermite interpolating polynomials. Matches both function values and derivatives at nodes.

LAGRANGE.description: Lagrange interpolating polynomials. Exact interpolation through specified nodes.

POWER_SERIES.description: Standard power series (monomial basis): c0 + c1*x + c2*x^2 + ...

POS_COEFF_X.description:
Position coefficients for X-axis (km).
Length must equal NUM_COEFFICIENTS. Ordered c0, c1, ..., c_{N-1}.

POS_COEFF_Y.description:
Position coefficients for Y-axis (km).
Length must equal NUM_COEFFICIENTS.

POS_COEFF_Z.description:
Position coefficients for Z-axis (km).
Length must equal NUM_COEFFICIENTS.

HAS_VELOCITY_COEFFICIENTS.description:
Whether explicit velocity coefficients are provided.
If false, velocity should be derived by differentiating the position polynomial.

VEL_COEFF_X.description:
Velocity coefficients for X-axis (km/s). Optional.
Length must equal NUM_COEFFICIENTS if present.

MAX_POSITION_RESIDUAL.description: Maximum position fit residual over this segment (km). Optional quality metric.

RMS_POSITION_RESIDUAL.description: RMS position fit residual over this segment (km). Optional quality metric.

PPEOrbitalElementRecord.description:
A single time-segment record of polynomial coefficients for classical orbital elements.

The six classical elements are:
1. SMA or R_PERIAPSIS (size/shape) — see SIZE_SHAPE_TYPE
2. Eccentricity (dimensionless)
3. Inclination (degrees)
4. Right Ascension of Ascending Node / RAAN (degrees)
5. Argument of Periapsis (degrees)
6. Anomaly (degrees) — see ANOMALY_TYPE

Evaluation follows the same normalized-time procedure as PPEPositionRecord.

EPOCH_MID.description: Midpoint epoch of this record's validity window (ISO 8601 UTC or TDB).

EPOCH_HALF_SPAN.description: Half-span of the validity window in seconds.

NUM_COEFFICIENTS.description: Number of polynomial coefficients per element.

BASIS_TYPE.description: Polynomial basis type for interpreting the coefficient arrays.

CHEBYSHEV.description: Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind T_n(x). Most common for ephemeris fitting due to minimax approximation properties.

POWER_SERIES.description: Standard power series (monomial basis): c0 + c1*x + c2*x^2 + ...

R_PERIAPSIS.description: Radius of periapsis (km). Preferred for hyperbolic orbits.

ECCENTRIC_ANOMALY.description: Eccentric anomaly (auxiliary angle in the Kepler equation).

COEFF_ECCENTRICITY.description:
Coefficients for eccentricity (dimensionless).

COEFF_INCLINATION.description:

COEFF_RAAN.description:
Coefficients for RAAN (degrees).

COEFF_ANOMALY.description:

Length must equal NUM_COEFFICIENTS.

Maximum element fit residual over this segment. Optional quality metric.
Units depend on the element (km for SMA, degrees for angles, dimensionless for ecc).

RMS_ELEMENT_RESIDUAL.description: RMS element fit residual over this segment. Optional quality metric.

PPE.description:
Polynomial Ephemeris — top-level message containing metadata and
one or more polynomial coefficient records for a single space object.

A PPE message may contain position records, orbital element records, or both.
Records should be ordered chronologically by EPOCH_MID and should collectively
cover the time span [START_TIME, STOP_TIME] without gaps.

CENTER_NAME.description: Origin of the reference frame (e.g., EARTH, MOON, MARS).

REFERENCE_FRAME.description: Reference frame for position/velocity coefficients.

TIME_SYSTEM.description: Time system used for all epochs in this message.

SCLK.description: Spacecraft Clock (receiver) (requires rules for interpretation in ICD)

START_TIME.description: Start of the total time span covered by this ephemeris (ISO 8601).

STOP_TIME.description: End of the total time span covered by this ephemeris (ISO 8601).

DEFAULT_BASIS_TYPE.description:
Default polynomial basis type for all records in this message.
Individual records may override this with their own BASIS_TYPE field.

CHEBYSHEV.description: Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind T_n(x). Most common for ephemeris fitting due to minimax approximation properties.

LEGENDRE.description: Legendre polynomials P_n(x). Orthogonal on [-1, 1] with unit weight function.

HERMITE.description: Hermite interpolating polynomials. Matches both function values and derivatives at nodes.

LAGRANGE.description: Lagrange interpolating polynomials. Exact interpolation through specified nodes.

POWER_SERIES.description: Standard power series (monomial basis): c0 + c1*x + c2*x^2 + ...

POSITION_RECORDS.description:
Array of position polynomial records.
Each record covers a time segment; together they span [START_TIME, STOP_TIME].

ORBITAL_ELEMENT_RECORDS.description:
Array of orbital element polynomial records.
Each record covers a time segment; together they span [START_TIME, STOP_TIME].

EPHEMERIS_SOURCE.description:
Generating ephemeris source, verbatim as the generator names itself
(e.g., a planetary ephemeris series designation, a numerical propagator
name and version, or an in-house tool identifier).

NOMINAL_SEGMENT_SPAN.description:
Fit span in seconds used to generate each polynomial segment.
Informational; actual spans are in individual records.

NOMINAL_NUM_COEFFICIENTS.description:
Nominal number of coefficients per segment.
Informational; actual counts are in individual records.

A single ephemeris data line (for non-uniform time steps only)
Use this format when time intervals between states are irregular.
For uniform time steps, use the compact EPHEMERIS_DATA array instead.

EPOCH.description: Epoch time, in ISO 8601 UTC format (required for non-uniform steps)
Epoch
