CONSTELLATION.description: Constellation

EPOCH.description: Observation epoch (ISO 8601)

ALTITUDE.description: Receiver altitude in meters above WGS-84

GNPName.description:
One name a place is known by, beside its primary NAME. Every attribute is
carried as the gazetteer publishes it; a consumer choosing a display name
applies its own policy over these flags and never has the choice baked in
by the publisher.

NAME.description: The alternate name verbatim, in its own script, unnormalized.

LANGUAGE.description:
ISO 639 language tag when the gazetteer states one. A gazetteer may also
state a non-language tag for a link or a postal, IATA, ICAO, or similar
coded name; that token is carried verbatim rather than discarded.

IS_PREFERRED.description: The gazetteer marks this as the preferred name for its language.

IS_SHORT.description: The gazetteer marks this as a short form.

IS_COLLOQUIAL.description: The gazetteer marks this as colloquial or unofficial.

IS_HISTORIC.description: The gazetteer marks this name as no longer in use.

VALID_FROM.description:
Period the name was in use, verbatim as the gazetteer states it. Not
normalized to RFC 3339: gazetteers publish partial and era-qualified
dates here, and coercion would invent precision.

GNPProvenance.description:
Dataset lineage and redistribution terms for one gazetteer place.

Required on every record: a redistributed place whose dataset, epoch, and
licence are unstated is not publishable. Dataset identity is DATA:
DATASET_ID, DATASET_NAME, and ATTRIBUTION carry verbatim what the gazetteer
states about itself. The standard names no gazetteer, dataset, or site.

DATASET_ID.description:
Publisher-stable, lowercase identifier for the gazetteer this place was
taken from, unique within the publisher's own dataset registry. Never a
display name and never a URL.

DATASET_NAME.description: The dataset's own name, verbatim as its publisher states it.

DATASET_URL.description: Replayable URL of the dataset as published.

DATASET_EPOCH.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond epoch of the dataset edition this place
was decoded from. The edition boundary, not the fetch: two records
carrying the same DATASET_ID and DATASET_EPOCH were cut from the same
bytes and are directly comparable.

DATASET_CID.description:
Content identifier of the exact dataset artifact, when the publisher
distributes one, so an epoch can be verified rather than trusted.

SOURCE_URL.description: Replayable URL identifying the source material within the dataset.

SOURCE_QUERY.description:
The exact query, filter, or file selection used, so the same rows can be
recovered by repeating the fetch.

LICENSE.description:
Redistribution terms verbatim. Required: there is no encoding for a
redistributed place whose terms are unstated. A dataset that publishes no
terms is recorded as publishing no terms; unknown terms are never public
domain and never an implied grant.

LICENSE_URL.description: URL of the full licence text as that dataset publishes it.

ATTRIBUTION.description:
Attribution text the licence requires a redistributor to display.
Required whenever the terms are attribution-bearing, which is the common
case for open gazetteers, and carried verbatim so a downstream surface
can render it without composing its own credit line.

NON_COMMERCIAL_ONLY.description: The licence forbids commercial use.

SHARE_ALIKE.description: The licence obliges derived works to carry the same terms.

NATIVE_ID.description:
This gazetteer's own row identifier for the place, verbatim. The join key
back to the source dataset; never re-minted by the publisher.

NATIVE_MODIFIED.description:
RFC 3339 UTC date on which the gazetteer last modified this row, as the
gazetteer states it. Distinct from DATASET_EPOCH: an unchanged row keeps
its modification date across editions, which is what makes incremental
sync possible.

GNP.description:
Gazetteer Named Place

One named geographic place as a gazetteer publishes it: its names, its
position on WGS 84, its feature classification, its administrative
containment, and the dataset edition and licence it was redistributed
under. The record is a NAME-TO-PLACE lookup surface — place search,
geocoding, and administrative resolution — and is deliberately not a
facility, station, or emitter record: $SIT carries an operational
facility, $GST a geodetic tracking station, $TBS a terrestrial base-station
site. A place gains meaning from those records by being joined to, never by
being conflated with them.

Positions are decimal degrees on WGS 84 and elevations are metres,
unconverted. A consumer needing other units converts at the join,
explicitly.

ID.description:
Publisher-stable identifier for this place record. Never the gazetteer's
own row identifier, which rides verbatim in SOURCE.NATIVE_ID.

NAME.description: Primary name of the place, verbatim in its own script, unnormalized.

ASCII_NAME.description:
Plain-ASCII rendering of NAME when the gazetteer publishes one. A search
and sort convenience, never a substitute for NAME.

ALTERNATE_NAMES.description: Every other name the gazetteer publishes for this place.

LATITUDE.description: Latitude in decimal degrees on WGS 84, positive north.

LONGITUDE.description: Longitude in decimal degrees on WGS 84, positive east.

ELEVATION_M.description:
Elevation in metres above the WGS 84 ellipsoid-referenced vertical datum
the gazetteer states, as published. Zero means unpublished, never sea
level; a place at sea level is distinguished by ELEVATION_PUBLISHED.

ELEVATION_PUBLISHED.description:
ELEVATION_M carries a published value. False marks a gazetteer that
publishes no elevation for this place.

DEM_ELEVATION_M.description:
Elevation in metres sampled from a digital elevation model, when the
gazetteer publishes a model-derived value beside or instead of a surveyed
one. Kept separate: a model sample is not a survey and the two must never
silently substitute for one another.

DEM_MODEL.description:
Name of the digital elevation model DEM_ELEVATION_M was sampled from,
verbatim as the gazetteer states it.

FEATURE_CLASS.description: Broad feature class this gazetteer assigns.

HYDROGRAPHIC.description: Hydrographic feature: stream, lake, sea, glacier, spring.

AREA.description: Area feature: park, reserve, oilfield, region.

POPULATED_PLACE.description: Populated place: city, town, village, capital, section of a place.

SPOT.description: Spot feature: building, farm, facility, church, mine.

HYPSOGRAPHIC.description: Hypsographic feature: mountain, hill, rock, ridge, plain.

UNDERSEA.description: Undersea feature: bank, ridge, trench, seamount.

UNSPECIFIED.description: The gazetteer names a class this enum does not model, or publishes none. FEATURE_CLASS defaults here so an unset field can never be read as ADMINISTRATIVE, which holds ordinal 0. The source token, when there is one, is still carried in FEATURE_CLASS_CODE.

FEATURE_CLASS_CODE.description:
The gazetteer's own class token, verbatim, so a class outside
gnpFeatureClass survives a round trip.

FEATURE_CODE.description: The gazetteer's fine-grained feature code, verbatim.

FEATURE_NAME.description:
Human-readable expansion of FEATURE_CODE, as the gazetteer publishes it.
A display string, never a key.

COUNTRY_CODE.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code, uppercase, as the gazetteer states it.

COUNTRY_NAME.description:
Country name as the gazetteer publishes it. A display name, never a key:
consumers key on COUNTRY_CODE.

ALTERNATE_COUNTRY_CODES.description:
Further ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes for places the gazetteer reports as
spanning or being disputed between several countries. Order carries no
precedence and no sovereignty claim.

ADMIN1_CODE.description: First-order administrative division code within COUNTRY_CODE, verbatim.

ADMIN1_NAME.description:
Resolved name of that division. Carried beside the code so a consumer
need not hold the division tables to render a place.

ADMIN3_CODE.description:
Third- and fourth-order division codes, verbatim. Gazetteers publish
these as codes only; a name is carried when one is published.

POPULATION.description:
Population as the gazetteer publishes it. Zero means unpublished, never
uninhabited.

TIME_ZONE_ID.description: IANA time zone identifier for the place, verbatim.

TIME_ZONE_UTC_OFFSET_H.description:
Offset from UTC in hours the gazetteer states for that zone outside
daylight saving, and under it. Carried as published; a consumer needing
an instant-correct offset resolves TIME_ZONE_ID against a current tz
database rather than trusting these.

TIME_ZONE_DST_OFFSET_H.description: Offset from UTC in hours under daylight saving.

SOURCE.description:
Dataset lineage and redistribution terms. Required: a place with no named
dataset, epoch, and licence is not publishable.

GPXLink.description: GPX link to an external resource

GPXWaypoint.description: A waypoint, point of interest, or named feature

ELEVATION.description: Elevation in meters above WGS84 ellipsoid

GEOID_HEIGHT.description: Height of geoid above WGS84 ellipsoid in meters

SAT.description: Number of satellites used for fix

AGE_OF_DGPS_DATA.description: Age of DGPS data in seconds

GPXTrackSegment.description: Track segment (continuous span of track points)

POINTS.description: Ordered track points in this segment

GPXRoute.description: Route (ordered list of waypoints for navigation)

AUTHOR_NAME.description: Person or organization who created the file

GGM02C.description: Appended: widely distributed coefficient sets carried by open astrodynamics toolchains. Append only; never reorder.

GST.description:
Ground/Tracking Station Definition — the geodetic identity and geometry of
one tracking station, sufficient to reduce a radiometric or laser
observation taken from it.

This is deliberately NOT $SEN. $SEN describes an SSA sensor site by
latitude/longitude/altitude with tasking plans and statistics; it carries no
terrestrial frame realization, no station velocity, no reference epoch, and
no antenna axis geometry. Station coordinates without a frame realization
and an epoch cannot be propagated for plate motion and are therefore not
usable for orbit determination.

STATION_ID.description: Stable station identifier as used by the operating network, e.g. "DSS-63".

OTHER.description: A network not covered above.

DOMES_NUMBER.description: IERS DOMES number, when the station has one.

CDP_NUMBER.description: NASA CDP / SLR site number, when the station has one.

FRAME_REALIZATION.description: Terrestrial reference frame realization of POSITION_* and VELOCITY_*.

OTHER.description: A realization not covered above; name it in FRAME_REALIZATION_NAME.

FRAME_REALIZATION_NAME.description: Free-text realization name, required when FRAME_REALIZATION is OTHER.

REFERENCE_EPOCH.description:
Epoch at which POSITION_* is valid, ISO 8601. Positions MUST be
propagated to the observation epoch with VELOCITY_* before use.

POSITION_X.description: Station position in the stated realization, metres.

VELOCITY_X.description:
Station velocity (plate motion) in the stated realization, metres per
year. Zero is a claim that the station does not move, not a default.

AXIS_OFFSET_M.description:
Distance between the two mount axes, metres. Zero for an intersecting-axis
mount.

ECCENTRICITY_X.description: Vector from the monument marker to the antenna reference point, metres.

ECCENTRICITY_FRAME.description:
Frame the eccentricity vector is expressed in, e.g. "XYZ" (geocentric
Cartesian) or "NEU" (local north-east-up).

TRANSMIT_BANDS.description: Uplink bands the station can transmit, e.g. ["S", "X", "Ka"].

RECEIVE_BANDS.description: Downlink bands the station can receive.

CLOCK_OFFSET_S.description: Station clock offset from the stated time scale, seconds.

CLOCK_RATE_S_PER_S.description: Station clock rate, seconds per second.

CLOCK_TIME_SCALE.description: Time scale the clock terms are referenced to, e.g. "UTC", "TAI".

VALID_FROM.description: Start of the interval over which this definition applies, ISO 8601.

VALID_TO.description: End of the interval over which this definition applies, ISO 8601.

SOURCE.description:
Provenance of these coordinates, e.g. "DSN 810-005 rev. E", an ILRS SINEX
file name, or a VLBI station catalogue identifier.

PPEPositionRecord.description:
A single time-segment record of polynomial coefficients for Cartesian position
(and optionally velocity). Coefficients are stored per axis.

To evaluate position at time t within this record's validity window:
1. Compute normalized time: tau = (t - EPOCH_MID) / EPOCH_HALF_SPAN
where tau is in [-1, +1].
2. Evaluate the polynomial basis of degree (NUM_COEFFICIENTS - 1) using
the coefficients for each axis.

Velocity coefficients, if present, follow the same evaluation procedure.
If HAS_VELOCITY_COEFFICIENTS is false, velocity can be obtained by
analytically differentiating the position polynomial.

EPOCH_MID.description:
Midpoint epoch of this record's validity window (ISO 8601 UTC or TDB).
Together with EPOCH_HALF_SPAN, defines the time interval:
[EPOCH_MID - EPOCH_HALF_SPAN, EPOCH_MID + EPOCH_HALF_SPAN]

EPOCH_HALF_SPAN.description:
Half-span of the validity window in seconds.
The full span is 2 * EPOCH_HALF_SPAN seconds centered on EPOCH_MID.

NUM_COEFFICIENTS.description:
Number of polynomial coefficients per axis.
The polynomial degree is (NUM_COEFFICIENTS - 1).
Typical values: 8-32 for high-fidelity ephemeris fits.

BASIS_TYPE.description: Polynomial basis type for interpreting the coefficient arrays.

CHEBYSHEV.description: Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind T_n(x). Most common for ephemeris fitting due to minimax approximation properties.

LEGENDRE.description: Legendre polynomials P_n(x). Orthogonal on [-1, 1] with unit weight function.

HERMITE.description: Hermite interpolating polynomials. Matches both function values and derivatives at nodes.

LAGRANGE.description: Lagrange interpolating polynomials. Exact interpolation through specified nodes.

POWER_SERIES.description: Standard power series (monomial basis): c0 + c1*x + c2*x^2 + ...

POS_COEFF_X.description:
Position coefficients for X-axis (km).
Length must equal NUM_COEFFICIENTS. Ordered c0, c1, ..., c_{N-1}.

POS_COEFF_Y.description:
Position coefficients for Y-axis (km).
Length must equal NUM_COEFFICIENTS.

POS_COEFF_Z.description:
Position coefficients for Z-axis (km).
Length must equal NUM_COEFFICIENTS.

HAS_VELOCITY_COEFFICIENTS.description:
Whether explicit velocity coefficients are provided.
If false, velocity should be derived by differentiating the position polynomial.

VEL_COEFF_X.description:
Velocity coefficients for X-axis (km/s). Optional.
Length must equal NUM_COEFFICIENTS if present.

MAX_POSITION_RESIDUAL.description: Maximum position fit residual over this segment (km). Optional quality metric.

RMS_POSITION_RESIDUAL.description: RMS position fit residual over this segment (km). Optional quality metric.

PPEOrbitalElementRecord.description:
A single time-segment record of polynomial coefficients for classical orbital elements.

The six classical elements are:
1. SMA or R_PERIAPSIS (size/shape) — see SIZE_SHAPE_TYPE
2. Eccentricity (dimensionless)
3. Inclination (degrees)
4. Right Ascension of Ascending Node / RAAN (degrees)
5. Argument of Periapsis (degrees)
6. Anomaly (degrees) — see ANOMALY_TYPE

Evaluation follows the same normalized-time procedure as PPEPositionRecord.

EPOCH_MID.description: Midpoint epoch of this record's validity window (ISO 8601 UTC or TDB).

EPOCH_HALF_SPAN.description: Half-span of the validity window in seconds.

NUM_COEFFICIENTS.description: Number of polynomial coefficients per element.

BASIS_TYPE.description: Polynomial basis type for interpreting the coefficient arrays.

CHEBYSHEV.description: Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind T_n(x). Most common for ephemeris fitting due to minimax approximation properties.

LEGENDRE.description: Legendre polynomials P_n(x). Orthogonal on [-1, 1] with unit weight function.

HERMITE.description: Hermite interpolating polynomials. Matches both function values and derivatives at nodes.

LAGRANGE.description: Lagrange interpolating polynomials. Exact interpolation through specified nodes.

POWER_SERIES.description: Standard power series (monomial basis): c0 + c1*x + c2*x^2 + ...

SIZE_SHAPE_TYPE.description: Parameterization of the first orbital element (SMA vs R_PERIAPSIS).

SMA.description: Semi-major axis (km). Standard for elliptical orbits.

R_PERIAPSIS.description: Radius of periapsis (km). Preferred for hyperbolic orbits.

ANOMALY_TYPE.description: Anomaly type for the sixth orbital element.

MEAN_ANOMALY.description: Mean anomaly (linear in time for Keplerian motion).

ECCENTRIC_ANOMALY.description: Eccentric anomaly (auxiliary angle in the Kepler equation).

COEFF_SIZE_SHAPE.description:
Coefficients for SMA or radius of periapsis (km).
Length must equal NUM_COEFFICIENTS.

COEFF_ECCENTRICITY.description:
Coefficients for eccentricity (dimensionless).
Length must equal NUM_COEFFICIENTS.

COEFF_INCLINATION.description:
Coefficients for inclination (degrees).
Length must equal NUM_COEFFICIENTS.

COEFF_RAAN.description:
Coefficients for RAAN (degrees).
Length must equal NUM_COEFFICIENTS.

COEFF_ARG_PERIAPSIS.description:
Coefficients for argument of periapsis (degrees).
Length must equal NUM_COEFFICIENTS.

COEFF_ANOMALY.description:
Coefficients for anomaly (degrees). See ANOMALY_TYPE for interpretation.
Length must equal NUM_COEFFICIENTS.

MAX_ELEMENT_RESIDUAL.description:
Maximum element fit residual over this segment. Optional quality metric.
Units depend on the element (km for SMA, degrees for angles, dimensionless for ecc).

RMS_ELEMENT_RESIDUAL.description: RMS element fit residual over this segment. Optional quality metric.

PPE.description:
Polynomial Ephemeris — top-level message containing metadata and
one or more polynomial coefficient records for a single space object.

A PPE message may contain position records, orbital element records, or both.
Records should be ordered chronologically by EPOCH_MID and should collectively
cover the time span [START_TIME, STOP_TIME] without gaps.

CENTER_NAME.description: Origin of the reference frame (e.g., EARTH, MOON, MARS).

REFERENCE_FRAME.description: Reference frame for position/velocity coefficients.

TIME_SYSTEM.description: Time system used for all epochs in this message.

SCLK.description: Spacecraft Clock (receiver) (requires rules for interpretation in ICD)

START_TIME.description: Start of the total time span covered by this ephemeris (ISO 8601).

STOP_TIME.description: End of the total time span covered by this ephemeris (ISO 8601).

DEFAULT_BASIS_TYPE.description:
Default polynomial basis type for all records in this message.
Individual records may override this with their own BASIS_TYPE field.

CHEBYSHEV.description: Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind T_n(x). Most common for ephemeris fitting due to minimax approximation properties.

LEGENDRE.description: Legendre polynomials P_n(x). Orthogonal on [-1, 1] with unit weight function.

HERMITE.description: Hermite interpolating polynomials. Matches both function values and derivatives at nodes.

LAGRANGE.description: Lagrange interpolating polynomials. Exact interpolation through specified nodes.

POWER_SERIES.description: Standard power series (monomial basis): c0 + c1*x + c2*x^2 + ...

POSITION_RECORDS.description:
Array of position polynomial records.
Each record covers a time segment; together they span [START_TIME, STOP_TIME].

ORBITAL_ELEMENT_RECORDS.description:
Array of orbital element polynomial records.
Each record covers a time segment; together they span [START_TIME, STOP_TIME].

EPHEMERIS_SOURCE.description:
Generating ephemeris source, verbatim as the generator names itself
(e.g., a planetary ephemeris series designation, a numerical propagator
name and version, or an in-house tool identifier).

NOMINAL_SEGMENT_SPAN.description:
Fit span in seconds used to generate each polynomial segment.
Informational; actual spans are in individual records.

NOMINAL_NUM_COEFFICIENTS.description:
Nominal number of coefficients per segment.
Informational; actual counts are in individual records.

ephemerisDataLine.description:
A single ephemeris data line (for non-uniform time steps only)
Use this format when time intervals between states are irregular.
For uniform time steps, use the compact EPHEMERIS_DATA array instead.

EPOCH.description: Epoch time, in ISO 8601 UTC format (required for non-uniform steps)
Epoch

OBJECT.description: Satellite name for the first object

CENTER_NAME.description: Origin of reference frame (EARTH, MARS, MOON, etc.)

REFERENCE_FRAME.description: Name of the reference frame (TEME, EME2000, etc.)

REFERENCE_FRAME_EPOCH.description: Epoch of reference frame, if not intrinsic to the definition of the reference frame

COV_REFERENCE_FRAME.description: Reference frame for the covariance matrix

TIME_SYSTEM.description: Time system used for the orbit state and covariance matrix. (UTC)

SCLK.description: Spacecraft Clock (receiver) (requires rules for interpretation in ICD)

START_TIME.description: Start of TOTAL time span covered by ephemeris data and covariance data (ISO 8601)

USEABLE_START_TIME.description: Optional start USEABLE time span covered by ephemeris data (ISO 8601)

USEABLE_STOP_TIME.description: Optional end of USEABLE time span covered by ephemeris data (ISO 8601)

STOP_TIME.description: End of TOTAL time span covered by ephemeris data and covariance data (ISO 8601)

INTERPOLATION.description:
Recommended interpolation method for ephemeris data.
Supported methods: Hermite, Linear, Lagrange, Chebyshev.
When set to "Chebyshev", parsers should use POLYNOMIAL_POSITION_RECORDS
for high-fidelity polynomial interpolation instead of interpolating across
discrete state vectors.

INTERPOLATION_DEGREE.description: Recommended interpolation degree for ephemeris data

STEP_SIZE.description:
Time interval between ephemeris states in seconds.
If > 0: Use compact EPHEMERIS_DATA array (times are implicit).
If 0 or omitted: Use EPHEMERIS_DATA_LINES with explicit epochs.

STATE_VECTOR_SIZE.description:
Number of components per state vector in EPHEMERIS_DATA array.
6 = position + velocity (X, Y, Z, X_DOT, Y_DOT, Z_DOT)
9 = position + velocity + acceleration (adds X_DDOT, Y_DDOT, Z_DDOT)
Only used when STEP_SIZE > 0. Default is 6.

EPHEMERIS_DATA.description:
Compact ephemeris data as row-major array of doubles.
Only used when STEP_SIZE > 0.
Layout: [x0,y0,z0,xdot0,ydot0,zdot0, x1,y1,z1,xdot1,ydot1,zdot1, ...]
Units: position in km, velocity in km/s, acceleration in km/s²
Length must be divisible by STATE_VECTOR_SIZE.
Number of states = length(EPHEMERIS_DATA) / STATE_VECTOR_SIZE

EPHEMERIS_DATA_LINES.description:
Array of ephemeris data lines with explicit epochs.
Only used when STEP_SIZE == 0 or omitted (non-uniform time steps).
Each line contains its own EPOCH timestamp.

POLYNOMIAL_POSITION_RECORDS.description:
Optional polynomial position records for high-fidelity interpolation.
Used when INTERPOLATION is "Chebyshev". Each record covers a time segment with
polynomial coefficients for continuous position (and optionally velocity) evaluation.
See PPE schema for record structure and evaluation procedure.

OEM Header

CCSDS_OCM_VERS.description: Format version in the form of 'x.y', where 'y' is incremented for minor changes, and 'x' for major changes.

MAN_UNITS.description: Units for the maneuver data values.

OD_PREV_ID.description: Identifier of the previous orbit determination.

OD_TIME_TAG.description: Time tag of the orbit determination.

OD_OBSERVATIONS_TYPE.description: Types of observations used (e.g., RANGE, DOPPLER).

Epochs aligned with OD_RESIDUALS_SERIES (UNIX timestamp) [numeric seconds
since 1970-01-01T00:00:00 UTC].

OD_ID of the batch baseline solution a filtered solution derives from and
is compared against (empty for batch solutions).

Post-fit residual RMS of the batch baseline, for direct batch-vs-filter
comparison.

TRAJ_TYPE.description:
Trajectory state representation type.
Determines how orbit state data is parameterized in this message.
For CARTESIAN_PV/CARTESIAN_PVA, use STATE_DATA array.
For POLYNOMIAL_POS/POLYNOMIAL_OE, use the corresponding polynomial record arrays.

CARTESIAN_PV.description: Cartesian position and velocity (X, Y, Z, X_DOT, Y_DOT, Z_DOT).

CARTESIAN_PVA.description: Cartesian position, velocity, and acceleration (9 components).

POLYNOMIAL_POS.description: Polynomial coefficients for Cartesian position (and optionally velocity). Associated data in POLYNOMIAL_POSITION_RECORDS.

POLYNOMIAL_OE.description: Polynomial coefficients for classical orbital elements. Associated data in POLYNOMIAL_OE_RECORDS.

HERMITE.description: Hermite interpolating polynomial representation.

LAGRANGE.description: Lagrange interpolating polynomial representation.

TRAJ_TYPE_DESCRIPTION.description:
Legacy trajectory type string for backward compatibility and extended types
(e.g., "PROPAGATED", "ESTIMATED", "FILTERED").

STATE_STEP_SIZE.description: Time interval between state vectors in seconds (required for time-series data).

STATE_VECTOR_SIZE.description:
Number of components per state vector.
6 = position + velocity (X, Y, Z, X_DOT, Y_DOT, Z_DOT)
9 = position + velocity + acceleration (adds X_DDOT, Y_DDOT, Z_DDOT)

STATE_DATA.description:
State data as row-major array of doubles.
Layout: [X0, Y0, Z0, X_DOT0, Y_DOT0, Z_DOT0, X1, Y1, Z1, ...]
Time reconstruction: epoch[i] = METADATA.START_TIME + (i * STATE_STEP_SIZE)
Length must be divisible by STATE_VECTOR_SIZE.

COVARIANCE_DATA.description:
Covariance data as flat array (21 elements per epoch for 6x6 lower triangular).
Time alignment matches STATE_DATA epochs.

POLYNOMIAL_POSITION_RECORDS.description:
Polynomial position records.
Used when TRAJ_TYPE is POLYNOMIAL_POS. Each record covers a time segment
with polynomial coefficients for X, Y, Z position (and optionally velocity).
See PPE schema for record structure and evaluation procedure.

POLYNOMIAL_OE_RECORDS.description:
Polynomial orbital element records.
Used when TRAJ_TYPE is POLYNOMIAL_OE. Each record covers a time segment
with polynomial coefficients for classical orbital elements.
See PPE schema for record structure and evaluation procedure.

ORBIT_DETERMINATION.description: Orbit determination data.

STOP_TIME.description: Stop epoch for compact trajectory and condition arrays.

STEP_SIZE.description: Uniform step size in seconds. Use zero when samples are epoch-tagged elsewhere.

ATMOSPHERE_COUPLING.description: Coupling mode used between the propagator and atmosphere provider.

FLOW_REGIME.description: Flow regime classification for the sampled trajectory.

STATE_VECTOR_SIZE.description: Number of position/velocity components per state sample.

STATE_DATA.description: Flat state array [x, y, z, vx, vy, vz, ...] in km and km/s.

SAMPLE_EPOCHS.description: Epochs for irregularly sampled condition arrays.

COL_INDICATORS.description: Column indicators for the hypothesis matrix

Observation epoch (ISO 8601)

IQCGeolocation.description:
Geodetic position of the receiver at capture time.

A separate table because latitude/longitude 0,0 is a VALID coordinate: an
absent GEOLOCATION means "the source published no position", which a
zero-defaulted scalar pair could never express.

LATITUDE_DEG.description: Geodetic latitude, degrees, WGS-84, positive north.

LONGITUDE_DEG.description: Geodetic longitude, degrees, WGS-84, positive east.

ALTITUDE_M.description:
Height above the WGS-84 ellipsoid, metres. Absent in most SigMF
recordings; SigMF `core:geolocation` is a GeoJSON Point whose third
ordinate is optional.

UNCERTAINTY_M.description: Reported position uncertainty, metres, when the source states one.

METHOD.description:
How the position was obtained, verbatim from the source (e.g. "GPS",
"station registry", "author-supplied"). Never inferred.

IQCHardware.description:
Receive chain that produced the samples.

Every field is a verbatim string. SigMF `core:hw` is free text and the
non-SigMF archives publish nothing more structured; splitting free text
into a manufacturer and a model by guessing is a defect.

DESCRIPTION.description:
SigMF `core:hw` verbatim, or the source's equivalent free-text
description of the receive chain.

MANUFACTURER.description: Receiver manufacturer, only when the source names it as its own field.

MODEL.description: Receiver model, only when the source names it as its own field.

ANTENNA.description: Antenna description, only when the source names it as its own field.

RECORDER.description: SigMF `core:recorder` — the SOFTWARE that wrote the recording.

IQCSegment.description:
One SigMF capture segment: the point in the sample stream at which the
listed tuning took effect. A retuned or frequency-hopped recording has
several; a single-tune recording has one.

SAMPLE_START.description: SigMF `core:sample_start` — index of the first sample of this segment.

GLOBAL_INDEX.description:
SigMF `core:global_index` — index of this sample in the receiver's
free-running sample counter.

HEADER_BYTES.description:
SigMF `core:header_bytes` — bytes preceding this segment in the data
file.

CENTER_FREQ_HZ.description: SigMF `core:frequency` — centre frequency of this segment, HERTZ.

DATETIME.description: SigMF `core:datetime` — ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of SAMPLE_START.

IQCAnnotation.description: One labelled region of the capture in time and frequency.

SAMPLE_START.description: SigMF `core:sample_start` — first sample of the annotated region.

SAMPLE_COUNT.description: SigMF `core:sample_count` — length of the annotated region in samples.

FREQ_LOWER_EDGE_HZ.description: SigMF `core:freq_lower_edge` — lower edge of the annotated band, HERTZ.

FREQ_UPPER_EDGE_HZ.description: SigMF `core:freq_upper_edge` — upper edge of the annotated band, HERTZ.

GENERATOR.description:
SigMF `core:generator` — the tool or person that produced the
annotation. An annotation asserted by an automatic classifier and one
asserted by a human are not interchangeable evidence; this field is how
a consumer tells them apart.

UUID.description: SigMF `core:uuid` — the annotation's own identifier, when present.

IQCExtension.description: A SigMF extension namespace the upstream metadata declares.

IS_OPTIONAL.description: True when the extension is declared optional for interpretation.

IQCPayloadRef.description:
A retrievable file belonging to this capture.

The record NEVER carries sample bytes. It carries where they are, how big
they are, and what they hash to, so a consumer can decide for itself
whether to fetch 400 kB or 127 GB.

DATA.description: The raw baseband sample stream itself (SigMF `.sigmf-data`).

METADATA.description: The upstream metadata document the record was normalized FROM (SigMF `.sigmf-meta`).

ARCHIVE.description: A container holding both (SigMF `.sigmf` tar archive, zip, tarball).

PREVIEW.description: A rendered spectrogram, waterfall, audio demod or thumbnail.

OTHER.description: A companion file the source publishes that is none of the above.

FILE_NAME.description: File name as the source publishes it.

MEDIA_TYPE.description: IANA media type when the source declares one.

BYTE_LENGTH.description:
Byte length. 0 means the source did not publish a size — it never means
an empty file.

BYTE_SHA256.description:
SHA-256 of the exact bytes, lowercase hex. Populated only when computed
or published; never guessed.

BYTE_SHA512.description:
SHA-512 of the exact bytes, lowercase hex. SigMF `core:sha512` is a
SHA-512 over the dataset file, so it is carried in its own field rather
than converted or discarded.

CID.description: IPFS CIDv1 when, and only when, this SDN pinned the bytes.

RETRIEVED_AT.description: ISO 8601 UTC time at which URL was last confirmed retrievable.

IQC.description:
RF IQ Capture Metadata.

The description of ONE raw, un-demodulated complex-baseband recording held
in a public archive — a hosted IQ-capture repository, a crowdsourced
signal-identification catalog, an institutional dataset repository, an
SDR project's capture database, a general-purpose research data archive —
normalized onto the SigMF v1 core namespace, which is the only metadata
vocabulary these archive classes share.

$IQC is a POINTER RECORD. It exists so a capture is discoverable, joinable
and verifiable without anyone mirroring its payload: the samples stay where
their publisher put them and `PAYLOADS` says where that is, how large it
is, and what it hashes to. `iqcCustody.PINNED` is a deliberate per-capture
decision for small high-value recordings, never a default.

UNITS ARE NORMATIVE AND NAMED IN EVERY FIELD. SigMF publishes frequency and
sample rate in HERTZ, so every frequency and rate field here is `_HZ` and
carries the Hz value unconverted. This standard deliberately does NOT
follow $RFB's MHz convention — silently rescaling a SigMF value on ingest
is the exact defect the suffix exists to prevent. A consumer joining $IQC
to $RFB divides by 1e6 at the join, explicitly.

LICENCE IS NEVER ASSUMED. An empty `LICENSE` means the terms are UNKNOWN.
It does not mean public domain, it does not mean permissive, and it does
not authorize redistribution. Crowdsourced catalogs and hosted repositories
both carry third-party recordings, so licence is per RECORDING, never per
archive.

Division of labour: $RFO = a sensor's astrometric/RF observation of a
tracked object (azimuth, elevation, range); $RFE = the parametric emitter
description; $RFB = the emitter's band specification in MHz; $IQC = the
archived baseband recording itself. $DPM remains the manifest under which
THIS network publishes a shard of $IQC records; it does not describe an
upstream third party's capture.

CAPTURE_ID.description: The upstream archive's own identifier for this capture, verbatim.

SOURCE_NAME.description:
Name of the archive that publishes the capture, carried verbatim as that
archive states it. A string rather than an enum so a new archive lane
never requires a schema release.

SOURCE_URL.description: Landing page for the capture at the source.

SOURCE_RECORD_ID.description:
Identifier of the source record this was normalized from, when the
source exposes one distinct from CAPTURE_ID.

SOURCE_SHA256.description:
SHA-256 of the raw upstream metadata bytes that produced this record,
lowercase hex. Makes the normalization auditable.

RETRIEVED_AT.description: ISO 8601 UTC time the source metadata was retrieved.

SIGMF_VERSION.description:
SigMF `core:version` — the SigMF specification version the upstream
metadata declares. Empty for captures normalized from a non-SigMF
source; that emptiness is itself informative.

COLLECTION.description:
SigMF `core:collection` — identifier of the collection this recording
belongs to.

DATATYPE.description:
SigMF `core:datatype` VERBATIM, e.g. "cf32_le", "ci16_le", "ru8". Never
re-spelled, never normalized to another vocabulary. A consumer that
cannot parse the token MUST refuse the samples rather than assume a
layout.

NUM_CHANNELS.description:
SigMF `core:num_channels`. 0 means unstated; 1 is the SigMF default and
MUST be written explicitly when known.

CENTER_FREQ_HZ.description:
Centre frequency of the FIRST capture segment, HERTZ, copied here for
indexing. `SEGMENTS` is normative whenever it is present.

FREQ_LOWER_EDGE_HZ.description:
Lowest occupied frequency across the recording, HERTZ, when the source
states it or its annotations bound it.

FREQ_UPPER_EDGE_HZ.description: Highest occupied frequency across the recording, HERTZ.

SAMPLE_COUNT.description:
Total complex samples in the recording. 0 means unstated — it is NOT to
be back-computed from BYTE_LENGTH unless DATATYPE and any header bytes
are both known.

DURATION_SECONDS.description:
Recording length in seconds, when stated or exactly derivable from
SAMPLE_COUNT and SAMPLE_RATE_HZ.

SAMPLE_OFFSET.description:
SigMF `core:offset` — index of the first sample in the recording's own
numbering.

METADATA_ONLY.description:
SigMF `core:metadata_only` — true when no dataset file accompanies the
metadata.

TRAILING_BYTES.description:
SigMF `core:trailing_bytes` — non-sample bytes at the end of the data
file.

CAPTURE_START.description:
ISO 8601 UTC start of the recording (the first segment's
`core:datetime`).

CAPTURE_STOP.description: ISO 8601 UTC end of the recording, when stated or exactly derivable.

LABELS.description:
Archive-level tags, categories or keywords, carried verbatim in whatever
vocabulary the publishing archive uses.

GEOLOCATION.description: Receiver position. Absent when the source published none.

SIGNAL_NAME.description:
Signal designation the source states, verbatim ("LoRa", "DVB-S2",
"ADS-B", "VOR"). Not an enum: these archives catalogue the whole radio
world, and $RFE's `signalModulation` is a radar-emitter vocabulary that
would force every civil waveform into UNKNOWN.

MODULATION.description: Modulation the source states, verbatim. Never inferred from the samples.

BAND.description:
Band designation the source states. Shares $RFB's `rfBandDesignation`, so
an HF or VHF capture is designated identically on both records.

OTHER.description: The source states a designation this enum cannot express. The verbatim designation MUST be preserved in NAME.

VHF.description: ITU-R V.431 very high frequency, 30–300 MHz. Appended 1.177.0.

HF.description: ITU-R V.431 high frequency, 3–30 MHz. Appended 1.177.0.

MF.description: ITU-R V.431 medium frequency, 300 kHz–3 MHz. Appended 1.177.0.

LF.description: ITU-R V.431 low frequency, 30–300 kHz. Appended 1.177.0.

VLF.description: ITU-R V.431 very low frequency, 3–30 kHz. Appended 1.177.0.

SHF.description: ITU-R V.431 super high frequency, 3–30 GHz. Appended 1.177.0 to close the decade ladder between the pre-existing UHF and EHF members.

NORAD_CAT_ID.description:
NORAD catalogue number of the transmitting spacecraft when the capture
is of a known space object. Joins to $CAT.NORAD_CAT_ID. 0 when unbound.

OBJECT_ID.description: International designator of the transmitting spacecraft, when known.

EMITTER_ID.description: $RFE.ID of the emitter this capture is of, when identified.

RFB_ID.description:
$RFB.ID of the band specification this capture exercises, when
identified.

LICENSE.description:
SPDX identifier when the source states one, otherwise the source's
licence name verbatim. EMPTY MEANS UNKNOWN TERMS — never public domain.

LICENSE_URL.description: URL of the licence text the source points at.

ATTRIBUTION.description:
Attribution/citation string the licence requires this record and any
derived product to carry downstream.

CREATED_AT.description: ISO 8601 UTC creation time of this record.

UPDATED_AT.description: ISO 8601 UTC last-update time of this record.

SUPERSEDES_IQC_CID.description:
CID of the $IQC this record replaces, when the upstream capture's
metadata changed.

IRMSource.description:
The source object a job is reading, and the validators that prove a resumed
read is reading the same bytes.

SOURCE_URL.description: Replayable locator of the source object, verbatim.

SOURCE_OBJECT_ID.description:
Source-native object, export, or product identifier verbatim, when the
provider names one independently of its locator.

SOURCE_CID.description:
Content identifier pinning the exact source bytes, when the source is
content-addressed.

MEDIA_TYPE.description: Media type of the source object verbatim as the provider states it.

TOTAL_BYTES.description:
Total length of the source object in bytes. 0 means the provider did not
state a length; it never means an empty object.

ENTITY_TAG.description: Opaque entity validator verbatim as the provider published it.

SOURCE_SHA256.description:
SHA-256 of the complete source object as 64 lowercase hexadecimal
characters, when the provider publishes one. Never computed from a partial
read.

SOURCE_VERSION.description: Provider-stated edition, revision, or release marker verbatim.

VALIDATOR_MATCH.description: What the publisher concluded when it last compared validators.

MATCHED.description: The publisher compared validators and they agree; resuming is safe.

MISMATCHED.description: The publisher compared validators and they disagree; the bytes behind the offset are not the bytes that were read.

UNVERIFIABLE.description: The source published no validator to compare. This is NOT a match: a publisher that cannot verify identity says so instead of assuming it.

VALIDATED_AT.description: RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp of that comparison.

IRMDecodeContext.description:
Everything a resuming reader needs to decode a chunk that does not begin at
offset 0. Required whenever NEXT_OFFSET is past the source's own header.

FORMAT.description:
Format token the decoder dispatches on, verbatim and lowercase, e.g.
`text/csv`. A consumer that does not implement the format refuses the chunk
rather than guessing at a layout.

HEADER_LINE.description:
The source's header line verbatim, exactly as it appeared at offset 0 and
excluding its line terminator. This is the field that makes chunk N>0
decodable; without it a headerless chunk parses to zero rows and looks like
a clean tail.

HEADER_BYTE_LENGTH.description:
Byte length the header occupied at the start of the source, including its
terminator, so a reader can tell a header-bearing prefix from a data row.

COLUMN_NAMES.description:
Column names in source order, when the publisher parsed them. Advisory:
HEADER_LINE is authoritative and a disagreement is resolved in its favour.

CHARSET.description: Character encoding label verbatim as the provider states it.

COMPRESSION.description:
Stream-compression codec applied to the source bytes, verbatim and
lowercase. Empty means the ranged bytes are read as-is. Non-empty means
NEXT_OFFSET is a position in the COMPRESSED stream and DECODER_STATE,
WINDOW and PARTIAL_RECORD are all required to resume.

DECODED_OFFSET.description:
Position in the DECODED stream corresponding to NEXT_OFFSET, when the
source is compressed. 0 with a non-empty COMPRESSION means the decoded
stream has not been advanced.

DECODER_STATE.description:
Serialized, pointer-free image of the decoder at the seam — the state a
codec with no restart point needs in order to have one. Opaque to every
consumer but a decoder whose stamps match exactly. Never partially applied.

DECODER_STATE_FORMAT.description:
Layout identifier of DECODER_STATE, verbatim, naming the decoder struct the
image was taken from. A consumer that does not know the token restarts.

DECODER_STATE_VERSION.description: Version of that layout, verbatim. Any disagreement restarts the job.

DECODER_STATE_BYTE_LENGTH.description:
Byte length DECODER_STATE is expected to have. Carried even though the
vector knows its own size, so a size disagreement is detectable BEFORE the
image is loaded into a differently shaped struct.

DECODER_STATE_SHA256.description: SHA-256 of DECODER_STATE as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.

DECODER_BUILD_ID.description:
Build identifier of the decoder that produced DECODER_STATE, verbatim, so
two builds of one codec version are still distinguishable.

DECODER_STATE_MEDIA_TYPE.description:
Media type of DECODER_STATE, so an unrelated decoder refuses it instead of
misreading it.

WINDOW.description:
The decoder's history window at the seam — the bytes that ARE the codec's
back-reference dictionary. Carried separately from DECODER_STATE because it
is bulk data of a size the codec fixes, not part of the struct image.

WINDOW_BYTE_LENGTH.description:
Byte length WINDOW is expected to have, for the same detect-before-load
reason as DECODER_STATE_BYTE_LENGTH.

WINDOW_POSITION.description:
Offset into WINDOW at which the codec will next write, when the window is
a circular buffer whose contents cannot be interpreted without it.

PARTIAL_RECORD.description:
The bytes of the record that straddles the seam: everything the previous
chunk decoded of a record it could not finish. A resuming decoder prepends
these to the next chunk's decoded output before parsing. Carried as bytes,
not text, because a seam may fall inside a multi-byte character.

IRMChunk.description: One chunk that was read and durably committed.

CHUNK_INDEX.description: Zero-based position of the chunk in the job's read sequence.

BATCH_ID.description:
Publisher-stable batch identifier the chunk's records were stored under,
verbatim, so a consumer can join the mark to the stored rows.

RANGE_FIRST_BYTE.description: First byte of the range that was read.

RANGE_LAST_BYTE.description:
Last byte of the range that was read. Interpreted per RANGE_MODE:
inclusive under INCLUSIVE_BYTE_RANGE, exclusive under OFFSET_LENGTH.

BYTE_LENGTH.description:
Bytes the read actually returned, which may be shorter than the range
requested.

CHUNK_SHA256.description: SHA-256 of the chunk's bytes as 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.

RECORDS_DECODED.description: Records the decoder produced from the chunk.

RECORDS_STORED.description:
Records the storage lane reported as durably committed. A chunk whose
stored count is 0 is not marked at all.

RECORDS_REJECTED.description: Records the storage lane rejected or collapsed as duplicates.

ATTEMPTS.description: Number of read attempts this chunk cost, including the successful one.

COMMITTED_AT.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp at which the storage lane
confirmed the commit.

IRMFault.description: The last unrecovered error, carried so a resumed run can refuse to loop.

CODE.description: Publisher-stable error code verbatim.

MESSAGE.description: Human-readable message verbatim; never a substitute for CODE.

CHUNK_INDEX.description: Zero-based index of the chunk the fault occurred on.

CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES.description: Consecutive failed attempts at that chunk.

OCCURRED_AT.description: RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp of the fault.

RETRY_NOT_BEFORE.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp before which a consumer must not
retry. Empty means the publisher states no backoff.

JOB_ID.description:
Publisher-stable identifier of the ingest job. Together with the publishing
key it is the job's identity across every mark it emits.

SEQUENCE.description:
Monotonic version of this mark within JOB_ID. Highest wins per publishing
key. Never reused, never decremented.

PROVIDER_ID.description:
Publisher-stable identifier of the data provider being read, verbatim.
Publisher data: it may name a real provider.

INGESTOR_ID.description:
Reverse-DNS identifier of the ingest module or flow that owns the job, so
two pipelines reading one provider do not share a resume point.

SOURCE.description: The source object and its validators.

IN_PROGRESS.description: Chunks remain; NEXT_OFFSET is where the next read starts.

COMPLETE.description: The source was read to its end and every chunk was committed. NEXT_OFFSET equals the total length when the length is known.

FAILED.description: The publisher stopped on an error it did not recover from; FAULT states what happened. The mark stays valid as a resume point.

ABANDONED.description: The publisher abandoned the job deliberately; it is not a resume point and a consumer restarts from offset 0.

INVALIDATED.description: The source changed identity underneath the job (VALIDATOR mismatch), so the position no longer refers to the same bytes. A conforming consumer restarts from offset 0 rather than resuming.

RANGE_MODE.description: How byte positions in this mark are addressed.

OFFSET_LENGTH.description: Half-open ranges expressed as a start offset and a byte count.

INCLUSIVE_BYTE_RANGE.description: Inclusive first/last byte positions, the convention of ranged transfer protocols: a chunk of `RANGE_FIRST_BYTE`..`RANGE_LAST_BYTE` inclusive.

PART_INDEX.description: The source is delivered as discrete numbered parts and byte offsets are not addressable; CHUNK_INDEX is the only position.

NEXT_OFFSET.description:
Byte offset at which the next read begins, in the SOURCE's own byte stream:
the compressed stream when DECODE_CONTEXT.COMPRESSION is non-empty, in
which case it is a record boundary only in company with the decoder state,
window and partial record. On an uncompressed source it is ALWAYS a
complete-record boundary, corrected backwards from the previous chunk's
byte budget. 0 is a valid value and means the job has committed nothing yet.

NEXT_CHUNK_INDEX.description:
Zero-based index of the next chunk to read. With PART_INDEX addressing this
is the only position.

CHUNK_BYTE_BUDGET.description:
Byte budget the publisher reads per chunk. Records the ceiling the job
actually ran under, which a host may have clamped below the configured one.

DECODE_CONTEXT.description:
Everything needed to decode the chunk at NEXT_OFFSET. REQUIRED in practice
whenever NEXT_OFFSET is past the source's own header; a consumer that finds
it absent there restarts from offset 0 rather than decoding blind.

LAST_CHUNK.description: The chunk this mark was advanced from — the last one durably committed.

CHUNKS_COMMITTED.description: Chunks durably committed by this job so far.

BYTES_COMMITTED.description: Source bytes accounted for by committed chunks.

RECORDS_COMMITTED.description: Records durably committed by this job so far, across every chunk.

TARGET_STANDARD.description:
Four-character standard code of the records this job writes, `$` included,
e.g. `$TBS`. Never a union ordinal.

RECONCILE_MODE.description:
Reconciliation mode the storage lane was called with, verbatim, e.g.
`append`. A chunked job never reconciles per batch: reconciling would delete
every earlier chunk as the next one arrived.

MERGE_POLICY.description: Deduplication or merge policy the job applied, verbatim.

FAULT.description: The last unrecovered error, when there is one.

CREATED_AT.description: RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp at which the job was created.

STARTED_AT.description: RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp at which the first chunk was read.

UPDATED_AT.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp at which this mark was published.
With JOB_ID and SEQUENCE this is the version key; SEQUENCE breaks ties.

COMPLETED_AT.description: RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp at which the job reached COMPLETE.

EXPIRES_AT.description:
RFC 3339 UTC fixed-millisecond timestamp after which a consumer treats the
mark as stale and re-validates the source before resuming. Empty means the
publisher states no expiry.

PLGFlowNode.description:
One node in a composed flow graph. A degenerate flow IS a module: a leaf
module leaves the flow-graph fields on PLG empty; a composed flow populates
them. This is how flows reuse the module schema rather than a separate one.

NODE_ID.description: Stable node identifier within this flow

PLUGIN_ID.description: Plugin id of the module this node invokes

DISPATCH_MODEL.description:

independently instantiated signed WASM node, and "host-capability" = a
generic host adapter.

CONFIG.description: Opaque per-node configuration (FlatBuffer or raw bytes; never JSON)

CANONICAL_TYPE.description:
Canonical SDS identity carried by the edge. NOT `required`: an edge may
be opaque by design (see OPAQUE), and a signer must never be forced to
invent an identity to satisfy the schema. A contract MUST carry exactly
one of CANONICAL_TYPE or OPAQUE = true; a contract with neither, or with
both, is invalid and MUST be rejected by the compiler that signs the flow.

OPAQUE.description:
The edge carries bytes with no SDS identity BY DESIGN — an
application-blind host-capability adapter (an HTTP body, a raw file
chunk) or a timer TICK frame with no payload at all. This is a deliberate
signed assertion of opacity, which is why it is an explicit flag rather
than an absent CANONICAL_TYPE: a missing type must stay distinguishable
from a declared-opaque one. An opaque edge is ineligible for the aligned
route, so ALIGNED_ELIGIBLE MUST be false when OPAQUE is true.

PLGFlowEdge.description: One directed edge wiring a producer output port to a consumer input port.

CONTRACT.description:
Exact identity/layout and compile-time representation policy. NOT
`required`: marking a NEW field of an EXISTING table required makes the
FlatBuffers verifier reject every $PLG buffer written before 1.0.13,
which is a breaking change to a ratified standard. Presence is enforced
where it belongs — the flow compiler MUST refuse to SIGN a flow whose
edges lack a CONTRACT, and a verifier MUST reject a signed flow edge
without one. Buffers predating 1.0.13 stay readable and stay unsigned.

Basilisk.description: DEPRECATED — owner law 2026-08-06 forbids vendor/org-derived names in a standard's vocabulary, and this member is one. Its ordinal is wire data and is therefore NEVER removed or reused, and renaming it in place would still be a breaking change for every published manifest; the sanctioned repair is to stop publishing it. Publishers MUST migrate to `PRIMARY_CATEGORY: PROPAGATION` (astrodynamics simulation and dynamics-modelling) and MUST NOT set `PLUGIN_TYPE: Basilisk` on new manifests. Consumers MUST render an existing record carrying it as `Propagation` and MUST NOT surface the member identifier in any user- facing label.

Unspecified.description: No family stated. Sits at the end of the enum rather than at 0 because this enum is append-only and `Sensor` already holds 0; it exists so a record can distinguish "the provider did not say" from "Sensor". A consumer MUST render an `Unspecified` module as ungrouped, never as a member of any family.

PRIMARY_CATEGORY.description:
The one ratified $CCT category this module is shelved under. This is the
category a storefront capsule, a library shelf and a breadcrumb show when
exactly one must be chosen. UNSPECIFIED means the publisher did not
classify the module; a consumer renders it ungrouped and never guesses.

This supersedes PLUGIN_TYPE for all storefront, library and search
surfaces. PLUGIN_TYPE remains on the wire and is not removed, but its
`pluginCategory` vocabulary mixes capability families with node-internal
plumbing, carries a legacy vendor-derived member, holds a real family at
ordinal 0, and admits only one value. Canonical migration, applied by a
publisher rewriting an old manifest:
Sensor->SENSORS_AND_COVERAGE, Propagator->PROPAGATION,
Renderer->VISUALIZATION_AND_RENDERING,
Analysis->MISSION_DESIGN_AND_ANALYSIS,
DataSource->DATA_SOURCES_AND_INGEST, EW->ELECTRONIC_WARFARE,
Comms->RF_AND_COMMUNICATIONS, Physics->SPACE_ENVIRONMENT,
Shader->VISUALIZATION_AND_RENDERING, Parser->DATA_SOURCES_AND_INGEST,
Validator->DATA_VALIDATION_AND_QUALITY, Interpolator->PROPAGATION,
Exporter->DATA_SOURCES_AND_INGEST, Foundation->FOUNDATION_AND_MATH,
Infrastructure->NODE_INFRASTRUCTURE, Licensing->COMMERCE_AND_LICENSING,
Storefront->COMMERCE_AND_LICENSING, Publisher->NODE_INFRASTRUCTURE,
Basilisk->PROPAGATION, Maneuver->MANEUVER_PLANNING,
Flow->FLOW_AND_COMPOSITION, Unspecified->UNSPECIFIED.
The mapping is one-way: PRIMARY_CATEGORY is never back-derived into
PLUGIN_TYPE.

UNSPECIFIED.description: No capability class stated. The publisher did not classify the unit. A consumer MUST render an UNSPECIFIED unit as ungrouped and MUST NOT infer a class from the unit's name, description or tags. Display name: "Unspecified".

PROPAGATION.description: Advancing an object's state forward or backward in time under a force model, and interpolating between computed states. Display name: "Propagation".

ORBIT_DETERMINATION.description: Estimating an object's state or model parameters by fitting to observations or ephemerides. Display name: "Orbit Determination".

MANEUVER_PLANNING.description: Planning, targeting and optimizing trajectory changes, including station-keeping, transfers and collision-avoidance maneuvers. Display name: "Maneuver Planning".

CONJUNCTION_ASSESSMENT.description: Screening for close approaches between objects and quantifying collision probability and miss distance. Display name: "Conjunction Assessment".

REENTRY_AND_BREAKUP.description: Atmospheric reentry, decay prediction, fragmentation and debris-cloud evolution. Display name: "Reentry & Breakup".

ATTITUDE_AND_POINTING.description: Attitude determination and control, body orientation, and pointing or slew planning. Display name: "Attitude & Pointing".

REFERENCE_FRAMES_AND_TIME.description: Coordinate frame realization and transformation, time scale conversion, and earth-orientation parameter handling. Display name: "Reference Frames & Time".

SENSORS_AND_COVERAGE.description: Sensor modelling and tasking, field-of-regard and access computation, and area or target coverage figures of merit. Display name: "Sensors & Coverage".

TRACKING_AND_OBSERVATION.description: Producing, correlating or associating observations of tracked objects, and maintaining tracks from them. Display name: "Tracking & Observation".

RF_AND_COMMUNICATIONS.description: Radio-frequency link modelling, emitter and band characterization, signal capture handling, and communications planning. Display name: "RF & Communications".

ELECTRONIC_WARFARE.description: Interference, jamming, spoofing and countermeasure modelling. Display name: "Electronic Warfare".

SPACE_ENVIRONMENT.description: Atmospheric density, gravity field, magnetic field, radiation, solar and geomagnetic activity, and ionospheric modelling. Display name: "Space Environment".

DATA_SOURCES_AND_INGEST.description: Acquiring bytes from upstream providers and parsing or exporting them across canonical record formats. Display name: "Data Sources & Ingest".

DATA_VALIDATION_AND_QUALITY.description: Validating records for integrity, physical plausibility, continuity and schema conformance, and scoring data quality. Display name: "Data Validation & Quality".

CATALOG_AND_IDENTITY.description: Object catalogue curation, cross-identifier resolution, bus and physical property association, and entity identity. Display name: "Catalog & Identity".

VISUALIZATION_AND_RENDERING.description: Rendering, scene composition, shading and interactive display of space data. Display name: "Visualization & Rendering".

GROUND_SEGMENT_AND_HARDWARE.description: Ground station operation and control of physical equipment, including antenna rotators, radios and other hardware interfaces. Display name: "Ground Segment & Hardware".

MISSION_DESIGN_AND_ANALYSIS.description: Mission and constellation design, trade studies, performance analysis and report generation. Display name: "Mission Design & Analysis".

FLOW_AND_COMPOSITION.description: Composition of other units into a graph. The unit of distribution is a flow of modules, not a leaf algorithm. Display name: "Flows & Composition".

DATA_STORAGE_AND_QUERY.description: Persisting, indexing and querying records; storage engines and query surfaces. Display name: "Data Storage & Query".

SECURITY_AND_IDENTITY.description: Key custody, signing and verification, authentication, authorization and access control. Display name: "Security & Identity".

COMMERCE_AND_LICENSING.description: Listing, purchase, subscription, entitlement and license enforcement for distributed units. Display name: "Commerce & Licensing".

NODE_INFRASTRUCTURE.description: Node runtime, artifact delivery, registry, publication and peer transport plumbing. Display name: "Node Infrastructure".

FOUNDATION_AND_MATH.description: Foundational mathematics and general-purpose utility libraries consumed by other units rather than run on their own. Display name: "Foundation & Math".

MDPEncounterStage.description:
One encounter stage of the body sequence: the set of bodies admissible at
this position in the sequence, and the epoch grid searched for it.

Bodies are named by NAIF integer ID, which is normative. SDS carries no
body enum and $GRV.CentralBody is gravity-model-scoped and incomplete, so it
must not be repurposed here. Note that a barycenter and a body center are
different objects (4 is the Mars barycenter, 499 is Mars) and the
distinction is operationally load-bearing.

STAGE_INDEX.description: Zero-based position in the ordered sequence.

ALLOWED_BODY_NAIF_IDS.description: NAIF integer IDs admissible at this stage. A single entry pins the body.

ALLOWED_BODY_NAMES.description: Advisory names, parallel to ALLOWED_BODY_NAIF_IDS when present.

EPOCH_WINDOW_START.description: Earliest and latest epoch searched at this stage, ISO 8601.

EPOCH_GRID_STEP_DAYS.description: Epoch grid step searched within the window, days.

V_INFINITY_MIN_KM_S.description: Bounds on hyperbolic excess speed at this encounter, km/s.

MIN_FLYBY_ALTITUDE_KM.description: Minimum admissible flyby altitude above the body's reference surface, km.

MAX_POWERED_FLYBY_DELTA_V_KM_S.description: Cap on powered-flyby delta-V applied at this encounter, km/s.

MDPFlightTimeBound.description:
Time-of-flight bound between two encounters. Adjacent stages give per-leg
bounds; non-adjacent stages give cumulative bounds such as
"Earth to Mars to Earth within 3 years".

FROM_STAGE_INDEX.description: Stage indices the bound spans. TO_STAGE_INDEX > FROM_STAGE_INDEX.

MIN_DAYS.description: Inclusive bounds on elapsed time between those two encounters, days.

MDP.description:
Mission Design Problem — the definition of a patched-conic broad search over
an ordered sequence of body encounters.

This is the PROBLEM, not a solution: it states what is being searched and
under what constraints. Candidate trajectories produced by solving it are
carried in $MDS. Nothing existing covers this: $LMS is a single Lambert
boundary-value problem with no body/epoch grid and no sequence, $MPE is an
Earth mean-element targeter, $MNF is an Earth manifold sweep, and $MNV is an
SSA-detected maneuver on a catalogued Earth object.

PROBLEM_ID.description: Stable identifier for this problem definition.

ENCOUNTER_STAGES.description: Ordered encounter stages. Order in this vector IS the body sequence.

MAX_TOTAL_FLIGHT_TIME_DAYS.description: Cap on total mission duration, days.

MAX_LAUNCH_C3_KM2_S2.description: Cap on launch characteristic energy C3, km^2/s^2.

MAX_TOTAL_DELTA_V_KM_S.description: Cap on total post-launch delta-V, km/s.

NONE.description: No deep-space maneuver on this leg.

MAX_DSM_DELTA_V_KM_S.description: Cap on the magnitude of any single deep-space maneuver, km/s.

DSM_GRID_STEP_KM_S.description: Grid step used when searching deep-space maneuver magnitude, km/s.

MAX_REVOLUTIONS.description:
Lambert controls: maximum number of complete revolutions considered on a
leg, and the admissible transfer direction.

OUTPUT_TIME_BIN_DAYS.description:
Output decimation: width of the time bin within which only the best
candidate is retained. Zero means no decimation.

MAX_THRUST_N.description: Optional spacecraft propulsion limits constraining admissible solutions.

EPHEMERIS_SOURCE.description:
Ephemeris source the search was posed against, e.g. a SPICE kernel set
identifier. Recorded so a solution set can be reproduced.

MDSEncounter.description:
One body encounter along a candidate trajectory.

Encounter-indexed rather than leg-indexed on purpose. A search implementation
typically emits leg-indexed arrays: for nE encounters there are nL = nE - 1
legs, the departure v-infinity of leg i is the OUTGOING vector at encounter
i, and the arrival v-infinity of leg i is the INCOMING vector at encounter
i + 1. Carrying both vectors on the encounter they physically occur at
removes that off-by-one from every consumer.

BODY_NAIF_ID.description:
Body encountered, NAIF integer ID (normative). A barycenter is not the
body: 4 is the Mars barycenter, 499 is Mars.

EPOCH_ET_S.description:
Encounter epoch as ephemeris time, seconds past J2000 TDB. This is the
form solvers work in and is carried verbatim to avoid a lossy round trip.

EPOCH_UTC.description:
Same epoch in ISO 8601 (UTC), for consumers that do not carry an
ephemeris time implementation. Advisory; EPOCH_ET_S is normative.

INCOMING_V_INFINITY_X_KM_S.description:
Incoming hyperbolic excess velocity vector, km/s. Absent at the first
encounter.

OUTGOING_V_INFINITY_X_KM_S.description:
Outgoing hyperbolic excess velocity vector, km/s. Absent at the final
encounter.

TURN_ANGLE_RAD.description: Turn angle between incoming and outgoing asymptotes, radians.

PERIAPSIS_RADIUS_KM.description: Flyby periapsis radius measured from the body's center, km.

POWERED_FLYBY_DELTA_V_KM_S.description:
Delta-V applied at periapsis for a powered flyby, km/s. Zero for an
unpowered (ballistic) flyby.

LAMBERT_SOLUTION_INDEX.description:
Index of the Lambert solution selected for the leg DEPARTING this
encounter, as reported by the solver.

FLYBY_SOLUTION_INDEX.description:
Index of the flyby solution branch selected at this encounter, as
reported by the solver.

MDSDeepSpaceManeuver.description: One deep-space maneuver on a transfer leg.

LEG_INDEX.description:

ARC_FRACTION.description: Position along the leg as a fraction of its flight time, in [0, 1].

EPOCH_ET_S.description:

DELTA_V_X_KM_S.description: Maneuver vector when the solver reports one, km/s.

NON_DOMINATED.description:
True when this candidate is non-dominated within the set. A set MAY carry

MDS.description:
Mission Design Solution Set — a set of candidate trajectories produced by
solving a mission design broad search, typically a Pareto front over
competing objectives (total delta-V against total flight time).

SDS had no multi-candidate container of any kind before this record. The
closest existing carrier for a single planned burn is OCM.Maneuver, whose
payload is untyped DATA:[string] with MAN_UNITS:[string] and which has no
v-infinity, turn angle, flyby periapsis radius, or C3.

PROBLEM_ID.description:
